As of Friday morning, Japanese fans were able to start playing the game, with many taking to Twitter to share their experiences.

The partnership with McDonald's is expected to bring a new level of excitement to the game, with the company's restaurants being designated as "PokéStops" or "gyms" where players can catch and train their Pokémon. However, in a bid to avoid any disruptions to customers, a McDonald's spokesman has urged players to be respectful of other patrons, stating that restaurants would "call on players not to become a bother to customers who are eating."

For many Japanese fans, the launch of Pokémon Go has been a long time coming. The game was first released in the US, Australia, and New Zealand on July 6 and has since become available in over 30 countries. The game's popularity has been unprecedented, with millions of people worldwide obsessively capturing and training virtual creatures in public spaces.

One of the first players to start playing the game in Japan was Samuel Lucas, an Australian YouTuber based in Tokyo. "The moment I found out the servers were up, I jumped right out of bed, got dressed, and ran outside with my iPhone and two extra battery packs," he told the BBC. Lucas's enthusiasm was matched by 21-year-old Tomoharu Kudo, who found a Charmander in his bed and then ventured out to explore the city for more Pokémon.

However, the launch of Pokémon Go in Japan has not been without its challenges. After weeks of stories about players in other countries getting into trouble while playing the game, Japanese authorities have taken precautions to ensure player safety. The National Centre of Incident Readiness and Strategy for Cybersecurity has issued a nine-point safety guide, which includes warnings about heatstroke, registering with "cool names" that are different from real names, and being mindful of one's surroundings while playing the game.

Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga urged players to abide by the safety guidelines, stating, "I want people to abide by the warning so that people can play it on smartphones safely." Unfortunately, just a few hours after the launch, there were already reports of an accident, with a student at Osaka's Kindai University reportedly falling down the stairs while playing Pokémon Go and being taken to hospital.

Despite the risks, Pokémon Go has proven to be a cultural phenomenon, with millions of people worldwide captivated by its unique blend of virtual and real-world gameplay. The game's use of augmented reality technology allows players to catch and train Pokémon in their everyday surroundings, from parks and streets to landmarks and public buildings.

The game's success is a testament to the enduring popularity of the Pokémon franchise, which first gained widespread recognition in the 1990s with the release of the Nintendo Game Boy. The trading cards that accompanied the game were a huge hit in school playgrounds, and the new game has managed to build on that legacy, introducing the beloved characters to a new generation of fans.

As Pokémon Go continues to take Japan by storm, it will be interesting to see how the game evolves and what new features and partnerships are introduced in the coming weeks and months. For now, Japanese fans can enjoy the thrill of the hunt, exploring their surroundings and catching as many Pokémon as possible. With its unique blend of virtual and real-world gameplay, Pokémon Go is sure to remain a global phenomenon for months to come.

A 45-year-old man from Ayrshire has been sentenced to a 12-month community payback order for assaulting his former partner over a period of seven years. Edward Barr pleaded guilty to assaulting Ann Begg, 51, at addresses in Cumnock and Auchinleck between May 1993 and May 2000.

The abuse began when Ms Begg became pregnant, with Barr becoming increasingly violent and controlling. Ms Begg told the court that the relationship was fine at first, but things changed when she became pregnant and was no longer able to give Barr the attention he demanded. She recalled being "pummelled" by Barr while pregnant after a row, and being dragged by the hair from the living room to the hallway.

The violence escalated over the years, with Barr pouring a plate of boiling hot custard over Ms Begg as she cooked a meal. The abuse eventually led to Ms Begg seeking refuge in women's shelters. The pair split up in 2000 when Barr started seeing someone else.

Lord Clark ordered Barr to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work as part of his community payback order. Barr has already spent the equivalent of eight months on remand. He was earlier cleared of 10 further charges of domestic violence due to a key witness failing to appear in court. Ms Begg had to give evidence against Barr at a trial in Livingston before his guilty plea. The sentence has brought an end to a long and traumatic period for Ms Begg, who has shown courage in speaking out against her abuser.

Local Photographer Wins Prestigious Award with Stunning Landscape Image

A breathtaking photograph of Loch Creran, taken by Hugh Nicol from Appin, has won the coveted Jolomo Colours of Scotland Photography Competition. The image, titled "The Audrey, Loch Creran," was captured during an evening cycle ride and showcases the serene beauty of the Scottish landscape.

Nicol, an estates manager in Argyll, is a self-taught photographer with no formal training. Despite his lack of experience, his photograph stood out among the competition, impressing renowned Scottish artist John Lowrie Morrison, who launched the competition last year. Morrison praised Nicol's image, saying it "shows the colours of Scotland extremely well" and "expresses a real feel of Scotland and a lovely feeling of movement."

The competition attracted a high volume of exceptional entries, with runners-up including Mairead Maclennan from North Uist, Susanne Wilson from East Kilbride, and Raymond Hosie from Campbeltown. Their photographs, featuring stunning landscapes from the Western Isles, demonstrated the diversity and beauty of Scotland's natural scenery.

Nicol's winning image was taken on a still autumn evening, when the loch's calm waters reflected the vibrant colors of the surrounding landscape. He attributed his success to the picturesque location, saying, "When you have somewhere as beautiful as Appin to work with, taking the picture was easy." Nicol's achievement is a testament to the power of amateur photography and the enduring appeal of Scotland's breathtaking landscapes.

Australian Scientists Stunned by Discovery of Ancient Volcanoes Off Sydney Coast

A team of researchers from Australia's national science agency, CSIRO, has made a groundbreaking discovery of a cluster of volcanoes approximately 250km off the coast of Sydney. The volcanoes, believed to be around 50 million years old, were uncovered during a search for larval lobster breeding grounds. This finding is significant, as it may hold clues to the separation of Australia from New Zealand, which occurred around 40 to 80 million years ago.

According to volcano expert Richard Arculus, "This is the first time these volcanoes have been seen." The discovery highlights the vast unknowns of the sea floor, with Arculus noting that the surface of Mars is better mapped than the ocean floor. The largest of the four volcanoes rises 700m off the sea floor, with a crater spanning 1.5km across. The discovery is expected to provide valuable insights into the Earth's crust and the composition of the underlying mantle layer. As Arculus explained, studying the volcanoes is like analyzing someone's "garbage bin" to determine their diet, offering a glimpse into the region's geological history.

A team of treasure hunters has begun excavating a site near the city of Walbrzych in Poland, in search of a legendary train said to be filled with loot and guns. The team, led by Piotr Koper from Poland and Andreas Richter from Germany, claims that ground-penetrating radar results are "very promising" and suggest that the train may be hidden in a tunnel. The dig is expected to take up to 10 days to complete.

According to local folklore, the armoured train was carrying gold from Wroclaw as the Soviet army closed in during World War Two. It was said to have gone missing near Ksiaz castle, just a few kilometers from Walbrzych. The Nazis had constructed a complex network of tunnels in the area, which were part of a secret military project that was never finished.

Despite the team's optimism, experts have cast doubt on the existence of the train. In December, Prof Janusz Madej from Krakow's AGH University of Science and Technology stated that a geological survey of the site had found no evidence of a train, saying "there may be a tunnel, but there is no train." However, the treasure-hunting team remains hopeful, with spokesman Andrzej Gaik saying that they need to find a railway track and the entrance to a tunnel to confirm the train's existence. The excavation has sparked widespread interest, with many eager to see if the legend of the lost train will finally be proven.

A 47-year-old man was found dead in a Compton Road bedsit on Monday at 20:30 BST. Despite treatment, he was pronounced dead at the scene. Police have informed his family and are questioning three suspects. Forensics experts are investigating the property, with a post-mortem examination to follow.

Education Secretary Justine Greening has announced that the government will not proceed with plans to remove the requirement for academies to have elected parent governors on their governing bodies. The proposal, which was met with widespread criticism from MPs, schools, and teaching unions, was included in the Education for All White Paper released in March. The plan aimed to give academies the "freedom" to choose whether or not to have parent governors, but it was seen as an attack on parents' involvement in their children's education.

Speaking to the Commons Education Committee, Greening emphasized the importance of parental involvement in school improvement. She stated that parent governors often play a "vital role" in turning around underperforming schools. Greening drew on her experience as a constituency MP, citing examples of schools that had improved significantly when parents became more engaged and invested in the school's success.

The initial proposal sparked an outcry from Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, who described it as an attack on parents. Former Prime Minister David Cameron defended the plans, claiming that they did not mean parents would be removed from governing bodies altogether. However, the backlash against the proposal was intense, with many arguing that it would undermine the role of parents in their children's education.

Liberal Democrat education spokesman John Pugh welcomed Greening's decision, saying it was a "climb down" from a policy that was "indefensible." Pugh criticized the government's education policy, describing it as "all over the place" and accusing ministers of being "ideologues" who disregard common sense.

While Greening has abandoned the plan to remove parent governors, she remains committed to her predecessor's vision of a fully academised school system. However, she has acknowledged the need to improve the financial accountability of these privately run but state-funded schools. The education secretary is currently exploring ways to increase transparency and accountability in academy finances, a move that is likely to be welcomed by critics of the academy system.

Greening's decision to retain parent governors on academy governing bodies is a significant concession to critics of the government's education policy. It recognizes the important role that parents play in their children's education and acknowledges the value of their involvement in school governance. As the government continues to develop its education policy, it is likely that the role of parents and the accountability of academies will remain key issues of debate.

Unrest Erupts in Kenya as Guinea Bissau Takes Lead in Qualifying Group

A contentious goal awarded to Guinea Bissau in the 81st minute sparked chaos in Nairobi, as Kenya's players and fans disputed the decision, claiming the ball had not crossed the line. The match was halted for 30 minutes as Kenya fans threw objects at the Guinea Bissau bench and the fourth official, prompting concerns about potential sanctions for the home team.

The goal, which proved to be the winner, gives Guinea Bissau a crucial 1-0 victory and propels them to the top of their qualifying group with seven points. Kenya, on the other hand, is now facing an uphill battle to qualify for next year's tournament, sitting at the bottom of the group six points off the lead.

In other Group E action, Congo and Zambia played to a 1-1 draw, mirroring their result earlier in the week. Jordan Massengo put Congo ahead just after halftime, but Winston Kalengo equalized in the 72nd minute. The result leaves Guinea Bissau in first place, with Congo and Zambia tied for second, one point behind.

Elsewhere, Ghana's perfect record in Group H was tarnished by a 0-0 draw in Mozambique. The Black Stars still maintain a four-point lead over Mauritius, but the latter has an opportunity to close the gap with a win over Rwanda on Tuesday.

In Group C, Benin thrashed South Sudan 4-1, with Stephane Sessegnon scoring twice, to take the top spot. Mali can reclaim the lead with a win over Equatorial Guinea on Monday. Meanwhile, Comoros suffered a 2-1 defeat to Botswana, just days after securing their first major qualifying win. The loss drops Comoros back down to earth, while Botswana moves level on points with the top two teams in the group, Uganda and Burkina Faso, who face off on Tuesday.

With all group winners guaranteed a spot at the 2017 tournament in Gabon, and the best two runners-up also qualifying, the competition is heating up as teams jockey for position. The outcome of the remaining matches will be crucial in determining which nations will secure a coveted spot in the tournament.

Former England football star Ray Wilkins has been handed a suspended prison sentence and a four-year driving ban after pleading guilty to drink-driving. The 59-year-old was caught driving his Mercedes in a bus lane on the A4 in London on July 1, where he also struck a kerb and was seen drinking alcohol from a bottle while behind the wheel.

Wilkins, who has two previous convictions for drinking and driving, was nearly three times over the legal limit when he was stopped by police. A passer-by had taken his keys to prevent an accident, and when officers approached him, they noticed his glazed eyes, unsteadiness on his feet, and the smell of alcohol.

The Uxbridge Magistrates' Court heard that Wilkins, who played 84 times for England, including at the 1986 Mexico World Cup, is currently undergoing a residential rehabilitation course at the Priory Hospital in Woking. His lawyer stated that he is "ashamed and embarrassed" by his actions, and Wilkins himself acknowledged that "abstinence is the only way I can control this situation".

District Judge Tim Boswell appreciated Wilkins' "genuine desire to change" and sentenced him to a 12-week prison sentence, suspended for 12 months. In addition to the driving ban and suspended sentence, Wilkins was ordered to perform 140 hours of community service. Outside court, Wilkins asked not to be judged on his alcohol problem, stating "I am an addict".

Drake Continues to Dominate Music Charts with "One Dance" and "Views"

This week, Drake has solidified his position as a leading force in the music industry, with his hit single "One Dance" spending its sixth week at number one on the singles chart. The song, which features WizKid and Kyla, has been a massive success, with 105,000 sales in the past week alone. Notably, about 75,000 of those sales came from streams, highlighting the growing importance of streaming services in the music industry.

Meanwhile, Drake's album "Views" has climbed three places to the top of the album chart, marking its second week at number one. The album outsold its closest competitor, Beyonce's "Lemonade", by just under 800 chart sales. This achievement is a testament to Drake's enduring popularity and the widespread acclaim for "Views", which has been praised for its introspective and emotionally charged lyrics.

In other chart news, Justin Timberlake's new single "Can't Stop The Feeling" entered the singles chart at number two, despite being at number one in the midweek charts. The song's success can be attributed to Timberlake's well-received performance at the Eurovision Song Contest, which helped to boost its profile. However, it was ultimately unable to surpass "One Dance", which held on to the top spot by a margin of just 6,000 sales.

The Stone Roses also made a notable return to the charts, with their new single "All For One" entering at number 17. This is the band's first new material in over 20 years, and its release was met with widespread excitement from fans and critics alike. Although it had been at number four in the midweek charts, it ultimately dropped to 17 by the end of the week.

Elsewhere on the charts, Calvin Harris and Rihanna's "This Is What You Came For" dropped to number three, while Sia's "Cheap Thrills" and Mike Posner's "I Took A Pill In Ibiza" remained at numbers four and five respectively. A second Drake song, "Too Good", featuring Rihanna, also appeared in the top 10, climbing 15 places to number eight.

On the album chart, Norwegian DJ Kygo was the highest new entry at number three with "Cloud Nine", while Meghan Trainor's new album "Thank You" debuted at number five. Justin Bieber's "Purpose" dropped to number 12, marking the first time it has fallen out of the top 10 in 26 weeks. Other new entries included Corinne Bailey Rae's "The Heart Speaks in Whispers" at number 14, Pierce the Veil's "Misadventures" at number 17, and Foy Vance's "The Wild Swan" at number 28. Kanye West's "The Life Of Pablo" also made its debut at number 30, following a rule change that makes albums available only on streaming services eligible for the charts.

Two suspected migrants were rescued off the Kent coast in the early hours of the morning after a lifeboat crew was alerted to their distress. The men, who had been at sea for over seven hours, were spotted by staff on a passing ferry, the Pride of Canterbury P&O, who noticed a weak light flashing from their mobile phone.

The lifeboat crew from Dover RNLI was dispatched to the scene, approximately a mile and a half off the coast, and brought the men to safety. They were found to be cold, shaken, and in a state of shock, having not eaten for two days. Paramedics treated the men at Dover Harbour before they were handed over to the authorities.

According to Andy Roberts from Dover RNLI, the men had called 999 for help at around 2:30 BST, but their location could not be determined until the ferry crew spotted the light from their phone. The Home Office has confirmed that the two men are now in the custody of immigration officials and will be questioned by Kent Police. A spokesman emphasized that border security is "paramount" and that authorities work tirelessly to "detect and deter" individuals attempting to reach the UK illegally.

Former Mercedes F1 boss Ross Brawn has revealed that he is providing consultancy services to Liberty Media, the company in the process of acquiring a controlling stake in Formula 1. However, Brawn was quick to downplay reports that he has signed a deal to run Liberty's involvement in the sport, stating that the company is not yet ready to make any definitive job offers.

Speaking to BBC Sport, the 61-year-old Englishman said, "Liberty have not got far enough down the road to make any commitments yet. I'm doing a little consulting to help them better understand F1 but that's all." This contradicts reports from Germany's Auto Bild and F1 Racing magazine, which claimed that Brawn had already signed a deal with Liberty.

Brawn's potential role in the sport's future is closely tied to the plans of current F1 CEO Bernie Ecclestone, who has been retained by Liberty Media for the time being. Ecclestone, 86, has reportedly been given a three-year contract, although this has not been officially confirmed. It is widely expected that he will eventually step down, with many believing that he will be replaced by at least two executives - one to oversee the commercial side of the sport and another to handle the sporting aspects.

Ecclestone currently has sole responsibility for both areas, including securing the sport's income from television contracts, race fees, and sponsorship, as well as playing a role in rule-making. Liberty Media's buy-out of CVC Capital Partners, which began in September, is expected to be completed early next year. One of the company's first concerns will be negotiating a new deal with teams, whose contracts expire in 2020. For now, Brawn's involvement remains limited to consultancy work, with his future role in the sport hanging in the balance.

A 34-year-old man, Craig Nelson, was found dead at the Woodhead Tunnels in Derbyshire. A post-mortem examination revealed he died from head injuries. Seven arrests have been made in connection with his death. Mohammed Bashir, 41, and Leonie Mason, 23, will appear at Sheffield Crown Court on Tuesday. Additionally, three 15-year-olds were arrested and released on bail. The investigation is ongoing, with South Yorkshire Police working to determine the circumstances surrounding Nelson's death. Further updates are expected as the case progresses through the court system.

Exeter Chiefs have completed the signing of 31-year-old Lewis Stevenson, who returns to the Premiership side after a two-year stint between 2007 and 2009. Head coach Rob Baxter expressed his delight at bringing Stevenson back to the club, praising his qualities and character. The signing comes as a response to long-term injuries to Damian Welch and Mitch Lees, which had left the team short on numbers. Baxter emphasized the need for quality players to maintain intense training sessions, which are crucial for the team's progression. Stevenson's return was made possible after he was released from his contract with Ulster by mutual agreement. The player expressed his gratitude towards Ulster, stating that he was proud to have been part of the team for five seasons. Stevenson's experience and skills are expected to bolster the Chiefs' squad, and he is likely to make an immediate impact.

Violence Erupts at Egyptian Stadium After Zamalek's Tournament Exit

A chaotic scene unfolded at Alexandria's Borg el-Arab Stadium as Zamalek was eliminated from the tournament after a 2-2 draw with Al Ahly Tripoli of Libya. The match was briefly halted when fans threw flares onto the pitch, causing a disruption in the game. The situation escalated after the final whistle, with seats being ripped out and thrown onto the field.

The Egyptian Football Association (EFA) has condemned the behavior of the Zamalek fans, with Karam Kordi suggesting that disciplinary action should be taken. However, executive manager Tharwat Sweilem downplayed the incident, stating that it would not impact the attendance of future international matches in Egypt. Currently, fans are only allowed to attend international matches, with domestic league games being played behind closed doors.

The incident is the latest in a long history of violent scenes at Egyptian football stadiums. The country has not allowed fans to attend league matches regularly since 2012, when over 72 Al Ahly fans lost their lives in clashes at the Port Said stadium. Despite this, the Ministry of Sports has announced plans to permit 70,000 fans to attend Egypt's 2018 World Cup qualifier against Uganda in September.

Celtic Energy has initiated a consultation on the future of its Nant Helen opencast site. This move follows RWE's announcement that Aberthaw power station will not require large coal volumes beyond March 2017. The company cites the struggling coal industry, stating "difficult decisions are inevitable." This news comes after Celtic Energy mothballed its Selar site, resulting in 70 job losses. The company is now reassessing its operations, including Nant Helen, due to market conditions. Trade unions and other parties are being consulted on the plan for the site's future.

Newcastle Falcons full-back Alex Tait is set to reach a milestone 200th appearance for the team. The 29-year-old, who joined as an academy player, has committed to a long-term deal at Kingston Park. Tait expressed his happiness at staying with the Falcons, stating he "didn't want to go anywhere else." Director of Rugby Dean Richards praised Tait's consistent performances, saying he "doesn't shirk away from hard work." This season, Tait has been selected 14 times in the Premiership, scoring two tries. Richards expressed delight at Tait's decision to pledge his future to the team, recognizing his value to the squad. Tait's dedication and hard work have made him a key player for the Falcons.

A popular dog walking spot in Dartford has been cordoned off after multiple dogs fell ill after entering Brooklands Lake in Powder Mill Lane. The Environment Agency has been notified, and vets are working to save the life of a fourth dog that became unwell. It is believed that the dogs were all being walked together when they became ill.

According to local reports, a total of seven dogs are being treated by a vet for "unidentified poisoning". The cause of the illness is still unknown, but police are warning people to stay away from the lakes as a precaution. Dog owner Chris Barnett reported that her Jack Russell, Millie, became ill after walking at the lake last week, but thankfully recovered the next day. Barnett expressed concern that someone may be intentionally putting harmful substances down for dogs to eat.

The Environment Agency is taking water samples from the lake, but so far, there is no evidence to suggest that any fish have been harmed. As a result, anglers are being warned to stay away from the lake until more information is known. Brooklands Lakes, a fishing venue run by Dartford Borough Council, has closed parts of the lakes and associated footpaths to pedestrians and dog walkers while the water is tested. The council expects the area to remain shut until the test results are known.

This is not the first time the lake has been closed due to health concerns. In 2013, the lake was closed after blue-green algae was found, which can be toxic to animals and potentially harmful to humans. The council is taking a cautious approach to ensure public safety and prevent any further incidents. Dog owners are advised to avoid the area until further notice.

Archaeologists Uncover Ancient Tomb in Northern Greece

A significant archaeological discovery has been made at the Kasta hill site in northern Greece, with experts believing that the tomb belonged to an important figure from the last quarter of the Fourth Century BC. The large mound complex, which has been unearthed over the past two years, is estimated to have been constructed after the death of Alexander the Great. Lead archaeologist Katerina Peristeri confirmed that the tomb dates back to this period, sparking widespread speculation about the identity of the person buried there.

The burial mound is an impressive 497m in circumference and was built using marble imported from the nearby island of Thassos. Some experts suggest that the renowned architect Dinocrates, a friend of Alexander's, may have been involved in its construction. The site has yielded several significant findings, including a lion statue that has been erected near the excavation site in Amphipolis.

The discovery has generated considerable excitement, with Greek officials hailing it as a major breakthrough. "The land of Macedonia continues to move and surprise us, revealing from deep within its unique treasures," said Mr. Samaras during a visit to the site. The find is the latest in a series of significant archaeological discoveries in the Macedonia region, which is also home to the tomb of Philip II, Alexander's father, unearthed in 1977.

A rare letter written by renowned author Beatrix Potter in 1937 has been sold at auction. The letter, signed Beatrix Heelis, was addressed to the mayor of Kendal, Henry Airey, and reassured him that she would take care of the town's last working loom, which she had just purchased. The lot also included a prayer book once owned by Catherine Parr, the wife of Henry VIII. The letter was put up for sale by descendants of Mr. Airey and was estimated to fetch between £1,500 and £2,000. The auctioneers described the letter as "a delight to read." Although the purchaser's name has not been revealed, the sale is a significant one, especially given last year's 150th anniversary of Potter's birth. Many of her beloved creations, including Peter Rabbit and Jemima Puddle-Duck, were written in the Lake District, where Potter drew inspiration from the natural beauty of the area. The letter provides a unique glimpse into Potter's life and connection to the region.
A 39-year-old man was arrested at North Lincolnshire airport after abandoning a stolen vehicle. Matthew George Dobson will appear in court, with airport operations remaining unaffected.

A bronze statue of rugby league legend Billy Boston has been unveiled in Wigan's Believe Square. The 82-year-old Cardiff-born player, who scored 478 tries in 487 games for Wigan, is the greatest try-scorer in British rugby league history. Boston, a pioneer for black players, signed with Wigan in 1953 and also played for Blackpool.

The statue, created by sculptor Steve Winterburn, is a fitting tribute to Boston's contributions to the sport and the town of Wigan. Wigan Warriors head coach Shaun Wane praised the statue, saying it is a "just reward" for Boston's achievements. Club director Kris Radlinski also highlighted Boston's charity work and dedication to the club and town.

The statue was made possible through donations totaling over £90,000, including a significant contribution from former Wigan Athletic chairman Dave Whelan and £3,000 from Wigan Council. Councillor David Molyneux, chairman of the Billy Boston Statue Trust, thanked all those involved in making the vision a reality. The unveiling ceremony was attended by Boston, who recently revealed he is suffering from dementia. The statue serves as a lasting tribute to his legacy and contributions to the sport. Boston's impact on Wigan rugby league is still celebrated today, and the statue will continue to inspire future generations of players and fans.

A wreath was laid in memory of Jimmy Hill outside Coventry City's Ricoh Arena by manager Tony Mowbray and goalkeeping coach Steve Ogrizovic. The ceremony, led by the Dean of Coventry John Witcombe, took place ahead of the club's Boxing Day match against Port Vale. Hill, who passed away last Saturday at the age of 87, had a profound impact on the club, serving as manager from 1961 to 1967 and later as chairman.

As a broadcaster, Hill presented over 600 episodes of Match of the Day and was a pioneer in the sport. He was also a key figure in the Professional Footballers' Association, leading the campaign to abolish maximum wages for players. Hill's legacy extends beyond Coventry City, with contributions to the sport including the introduction of the first all-seater stadium, electronic scoreboard, and colour match-day programme. The Football League remembered him as a "visionary" and "all-time great" in English football. His influence will be deeply felt, and he will be remembered as one of the most influential figures in the sport. The ceremony was a fitting tribute to a man who dedicated his life to football.

Mountaineer Leslie Binns is set to return to Nepal in April to tackle Mount Everest once again, after his previous attempt was cut short when he saved the life of an Indian woman. Mr Binns, 42, from Rotherham, South Yorkshire, was just 500m from the summit in May when he encountered Sunita Hazra, who was slipping down the mountain.

The former Army soldier, who lost vision in his left eye after being hit by an improvised explosive device in 2009, quickly sprang into action, using his military training to rugby tackle Mrs Hazra and prevent her from falling further. He then escorted her down to a camp, where she received treatment for frostbite. Mrs Hazra has since made a full recovery, thanks to Mr Binns' bravery and selflessness.

Despite being forced to abandon his own summit bid, Mr Binns said he has no regrets about his decision. "I've managed to save a woman's life and get her back to her family, so that more than makes up for it," he told BBC Radio Sheffield. Mr Binns will be returning to Everest in April, not only to fulfill his lifelong dream of reaching the summit, but also to raise money for a charity that helped him to retrain after he was medically discharged from the Army. He described the challenge ahead as "the hardest thing I've ever done in my entire life", but is determined to succeed.

A Labour-run council in Yorkshire has unveiled plans to cut various services due to significant budget reductions. The council's budget has been slashed by £144m since 2011, with a further £15.4m to be cut by 2018. Additionally, £11.5m must be found for social care over the same period. To achieve these savings, the council proposes to reduce the frequency of street cleaning, which will save £159,000, and scrap its dedicated fly-tipping removal team.

The number of children's play areas will also be reduced, resulting in a saving of £54,000. Furthermore, the closure of Knottingley Sports Centre and Castleford Swimming Pool is expected to save £650,000. The council plans to cut 100 full-time posts from its workforce of 4,916. To generate additional revenue, a 1.99% council tax increase and a 3% adult social care precept are being proposed.

Council leader Peter Box acknowledged that the decisions are tough, but emphasized that the welfare of residents remains a top priority. The proposals will be discussed by the cabinet on February 14 and, if approved, will be presented to the full council on February 28. The cuts are expected to have a major impact on nearly all council services, affecting various aspects of community life.

A member of the Qatari elite, Sheikh Khalid Hamad Al-Thani, is at the center of a reckless driving investigation in Beverly Hills, Los Angeles. A video, which has gone viral with over 1.2 million views, shows a yellow Ferrari, allegedly owned by Al-Thani, racing a white Porsche down residential streets, disregarding a stop sign. The footage ends with the Ferrari's engine smoking as it pulls into a driveway in an affluent neighborhood.

Police were considering charging Al-Thani with reckless driving and other offenses before he, and his cars, disappeared. Although Al-Thani has been dubbed the "patron sheikh" of drag racing and has given millions to Al-Anabi Racing, it is unclear whether he is a member of Qatar's royal family.

The Beverly Hills police department stated that the cars in the video were driving recklessly, but officers who arrived at the scene were unable to make an arrest or issue a citation as they hadn't witnessed the incident. Investigators have connected Al-Thani to the car, but they are yet to confirm whether he was driving either vehicle, as the drivers' faces weren't clear in the footage.

The investigation took a surprising turn when someone involved claimed diplomatic immunity. However, Lieutenant Lincoln Hoshino, a spokesman for the Beverly Hills police, said that the car was not registered with the State Department to be brought into the US, making it unlikely that Al-Thani had diplomatic immunity. Beverly Hills Police Chief Dominick Rivetti warned that claiming diplomatic immunity without having it is a federal offense and that they are looking into the matter. The Qatari consulate has been contacted, and authorities may pursue prosecution against those involved.

A massive fire broke out at the Baitul Futuh Mosque in Morden, London, on [date], with 70 firefighters battling to bring the blaze under control. The mosque, which is the largest in western Europe, has a community centre attached and serves the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community. Fortunately, the fire was contained to an administration building, and the mosque itself was unaffected.

The London Fire Brigade was called to the scene at 12:00 BST, and crews worked tirelessly to minimize the spread of the fire. By 17:30 BST, the blaze was under control, but not before it had caused significant damage to the administration building. Approximately 50% of the ground floor, part of the first floor, and a section of the roof were damaged in the fire.

A man was taken to hospital suffering from smoke inhalation, but fortunately, only a handful of worshippers were inside the mosque when the fire started, and they were quickly evacuated. The fire crews were expected to remain on site into the evening, damping down and dealing with the aftermath of the blaze.

Station manager Philip Morton praised the efforts of the firefighters, saying, "This is a large fire, and our crews are working hard to minimize fire spread to other parts of the mosque. We are working closely with the local community to ensure our damage control operations take full regard of the religious significance of the building's contents."

The Ahmadiyya Muslim Community was shaken by the incident, with Fareed Ahmed saying, "It's a very difficult time, and obviously, we're praying that it comes to a safe conclusion. This is a devastating accident to happen to any mosque." However, he confirmed that the mosque itself, where prayers take place, was safe and untouched by the fire.

Merton Council leader Stephen Alambritis described the mosque as a "beautiful building" and a "major landmark" in the area. He suggested that the fire may have been caused by cooking preparations rather than an arson attack, as the mosque is manned by security staff.

The incident has sparked an outpouring of support from the community, with Lord Ahmad, a high-profile member of the Ahmadiyya community and junior government minister, tweeting, "This is a beautiful mosque complex which has transcended barriers and been a beacon of peace - thoughts & prayers." The community is grateful that the fire was contained, and the mosque itself was spared, but the incident serves as a reminder of the importance of fire safety and the need for vigilance in preventing such incidents.

Andy Murray's Quarter-Final Loss Sparks Concerns Over His Future in Tennis

The tennis world was left stunned as Andy Murray, the 30-year-old world number one, suffered a devastating quarter-final loss to Sam Querrey at Wimbledon. The defeat has raised concerns over Murray's hip injury, which appears to have caught up with him, and his fellow Scot, Jamie Baker, believes that Murray may be forced to consider a lay-off if he cannot regain full fitness in time for the US Open in six weeks.

Baker, who has been following Murray's career closely, thinks that the Scot's primary focus should be on major titles, and if he is not 100% fit for the US Open, he may need to take a break to ensure he can compete at the highest level. "It has to all be about major titles, so if he can't be 100% for that, the next chance is Australia," Baker said. "So if he thinks getting 100% fit for that to have a chance of the title is a question of having three or four months off, then I'm sure he won't be ruling that out."

Murray's coaching team had been working towards a short-term goal of defending his Wimbledon title, but Baker believes that they will now need to take a longer-term view. "Obviously, he's in his early 30s and playing at Wimbledon is something he's not going to be able to do every year for the rest of his life, so you don't withdraw from here as defending champion without thinking about it very hard," Baker told BBC Scotland.

The hip injury has been a nagging concern for Murray, and Baker thinks that it may be a sign of a more significant issue. "On the other hand, for him to miss two or three days of practice in the week building up to a grand slam is also very unusual for him, so there definitely was something there," Baker said. "It's very disappointing for him, but obviously, he still has a good few years left at the top of the game provided he can stay fit and hungry, which I'm sure he will."

Murray's situation is not unique, as tennis legends Roger Federer and Rafa Nadal have both returned to form after extended injury lay-offs last season. Federer and Nadal have won the first two grand slams of the year, and Baker believes that their examples may inspire Murray to consider taking a break to regain his fitness. "When Federer and Nadal took that time off, I don't think any of us would have predicted that they were going to get back right to the top of the game like they have done," Baker added. "They've won the first two grand slams at the start of this year, so I think for Andy Murray that's certainly not something that you would think he was thinking of taking a long break. But, having seen the other two do that, it might be something he considers."

As Murray navigates this challenging period in his career, he will also be preparing for the arrival of his second child. Baker thinks that taking a break from the tour could be beneficial for Murray, allowing him to spend time with his family and recharge his batteries. "To have a bit of a break from the tour, get the body right, spend a bit of time at home with the family - he has a second child coming - maybe that will actually re-energize and put him in a fantastic position for the next three or four years potentially to challenge for these big titles," Baker said.

Ultimately, the decision on Murray's future will depend on the severity of his injury and his own ambitions. As Baker noted, "We don't know - and he probably doesn't know - how bad the injury is at this point." One thing is certain, however: Murray's fans will be eagerly awaiting his return to the court, hoping that he can regain his fitness and continue to compete at the highest level.

New Golf Degree Tees Off at University of the Highlands and Islands

A new BA honours qualification in golf is set to launch at the University of the Highlands and Islands (UHI) in partnership with the prestigious Royal Dornoch Golf Club in Sutherland. The four-year degree, which will commence in September, will provide students with a comprehensive education in performance, coaching, and equipment, preparing them for a career in the golf industry.

The course has received high praise from golf legend Jack Nicklaus, who has won a record 18 major championships. Nicklaus expressed his support for the initiative, stating that Royal Dornoch has a rich history in golf and a legacy in developing the game. He added that he fully supports UHI and Royal Dornoch in their efforts to provide education within the golf industry.

To be eligible for the course, students must have a current golf handicap of 4.4 or lower for men and 6.4 or lower for ladies. The degree will be based at the Dornoch campus of North Highland College UHI, which is conveniently located next to Royal Dornoch Golf Club's championship course, ranked sixth in the world by Golf Digest last year.

Former European Tour golfer Lesley Mackay has joined UHI as a lecturer and will play a key role in developing and delivering the new degree programme. Mackay described the course as "exciting, enterprising, and innovative," offering aspiring golfers the opportunity to reach their potential both on and off the course. Neil Hampton, general manager of Royal Dornoch Golf Club, also expressed his enthusiasm for the new course, stating that it will provide young people with a chance to make a career in golf, whether as a player, coach, or administrator. With its unique blend of academic and practical training, this new degree is set to be a hole-in-one for golf enthusiasts and aspiring professionals alike.

Legia fans sparked chaos on Wednesday, using pepper spray on security and setting off fireworks. Racist chanting allegations were denied by the club. Uefa charged Dortmund for similar fan misconduct. The governing body will review the cases on September 28, following the volatile Champions League tie. An apology was issued by the club on Thursday.

The Serpentine Gallery in London is set to unveil its latest annual Pavilion, designed by Chilean architect Smiljan Radic. The temporary structure, which will be situated on the gallery's lawn in Kensington Gardens, will be open to the public from June 26 to October 19. Radic's design features a translucent, shell-like building that rests on a series of boulders, creating a unique and intriguing space that will house a cafe and host the Serpentine's Park Nights series of events.

This year's Pavilion is the latest in a long line of innovative designs, which have been created by some of the world's most renowned architects and artists, including Zaha Hadid, Ai Weiwei, and Jean Nouvel. Radic's building, which occupies 350 square meters, is designed to be an interactive space that encourages visitors to explore and engage with its unique interior. The architect has described the structure as having an "empty patio" at its center, which will give the illusion that the entire volume is floating.

At night, the Pavilion will be illuminated with an amber-tinted light, making it a striking feature of the surrounding landscape. Radic has said that he was inspired by fragile, temporary structures such as roadside stalls, and that he is excited to have been given the opportunity to create something so innovative and experimental. The Serpentine's director, Julia Peyton-Jones, has praised Radic's design as "excitingly futuristic," saying that it "appears like an alien space pod that has come to rest on a Neolithic site." With over 300,000 visitors expected to attend, this year's Pavilion is set to be another huge success for the Serpentine Gallery.

A second vigil has been held in Glasgow to remember Karen Buckley, the 24-year-old student who was found murdered on a farm near the city last week. The event, entitled "Vigil For Our Neighbour Karen Buckley", took place in the Garnethill area where Miss Buckley lived and was attended by local residents who wanted to pay their respects to one of their own.

The vigil followed a similar event on Friday in George Square, which was attended by hundreds of people, including Miss Buckley's family. At Saturday's gathering, candles were lit in the shape of a triskele, a Celtic triple spiral, in recognition of Miss Buckley's Irish roots.

Miss Buckley, a student at Glasgow Caledonian University, went missing on a night out and her body was found four days later. Alexander Pacteau, 21, has been charged with her murder and was remanded in custody after appearing in court.

The vigils have been an opportunity for people to come together and remember Miss Buckley, who was described as a kind and gentle person. Her family, including her parents Marian and John, and her brothers, have been overwhelmed by the outpouring of support and tributes to their daughter.

A fundraising page set up by Miss Buckley's former classmates has raised over £50,000 to support her family, and a special prayer service was held near her home in Mallow, Ireland, earlier this week. The community in Glasgow has rallied around the family, with many leaving cards, flowers, and messages of condolence. The vigils have been a powerful way for people to show their respect and solidarity with Miss Buckley's loved ones.

Southampton Manager Ronald Koeman has warned midfielder Morgan Schneiderlin over his future conduct after the player expressed his frustration on social media. Schneiderlin, 24, tweeted "Six years of an amazing journey #saintsfc destroyed in one hour!" sparking speculation about his future at the club. However, Koeman has reaffirmed that Schneiderlin is not for sale, despite being linked to Tottenham.

Saints chairman Ralph Krueger has also stated that Schneiderlin and injured forward Jay Rodriguez will not be leaving St Mary's, following the sale of five players this summer. Koeman expects Schneiderlin to return to the side for the pre-season game against Bayer Leverkusen on August 9. "He is OK, he will play next week," Koeman said. "I spoke with him about that tweet. Always you have to keep that type of information inside and we spoke about that and his situation."

Meanwhile, Koeman has revealed that the club is close to signing three new players, adding to recent recruits Dusan Tadic, Graziano Pelle, and Ryan Bertrand. The Dutchman is also considering a swap deal involving club record-signing Dani Osvaldo and Inter Milan's Saphir Taider. "We are looking for the best for Osvaldo and the best for the club," Koeman said. "Taider brings quality and we need that. We need competition in the squad as well and that will be good." With two weeks to prepare for the Liverpool game, Koeman is hopeful of completing the new signings this weekend.

UEFA has unveiled the shortlist for its Team of the Year, with a total of 40 players from across Europe's top leagues vying for a spot in the esteemed lineup. The list features 12 Premier League players, including Leicester City's Riyad Mahrez and N'Golo Kante, who played a crucial role in the club's historic Premier League win. Other notable Premier League players on the shortlist include Toby Alderweireld, Laurent Koscielny, Paul Pogba, Kevin de Bruyne, and Sergio Aguero.

Real Madrid dominates the list with eight players, including Cristiano Ronaldo, Gareth Bale, and Luka Modric, following their Champions League triumph. Barcelona is also well-represented with five players, including Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez, and Neymar. The shortlist is divided into four goalkeepers, 12 defenders, 12 midfielders, and 12 forwards.

Fans can now vote for their preferred team on UEFA's website until January 3. The final team will be announced shortly after. Joe Allen and Aaron Ramsey are among the midfielders hoping to make the cut, along with other top talents like Andres Iniesta, Toni Kroos, and Dimitri Payet. With such a talented pool of players, the competition is expected to be fierce. UEFA's Team of the Year is one of the most prestigious honors in European football, and fans will be eager to see which players make the final cut.

Pakistani cricketer Asif has been cleared of a suspect bowling action. The 30-year-old underwent independent testing in Chennai, India, following a report after his second ODI appearance against Zimbabwe. All his deliveries were found to be within the permitted 15-degree elbow extension limit. Asif, who is uncapped in Tests, may make his debut in the final Test against England at Sharjah on Sunday if selected as a third spinner, due to Imran Khan's injury. Asif was recently called up to the Pakistan Test squad and his clearance comes as a relief ahead of the upcoming match.

Mario Balotelli is set to join AC Milan from Manchester City after the Italian striker underwent a medical with the seven-time European champions. The 22-year-old will move to Milan for an initial fee of 22m euros (£19m), pending the successful completion of his medical. 

Balotelli expressed his excitement about joining his new club, stating, "I'd wanted to play for Milan for such a long time." He acknowledged that he had previously played for other teams, but jumped at the opportunity to join Milan when it arose. 

The striker's departure from Manchester City comes after a tumultuous period, including a recent incident on 3 January. During his time at City, Balotelli scored 30 goals in 80 appearances and helped the team win the Premier League title last season. However, his form has been inconsistent this season, with only three goals in 20 matches. 

AC Milan's vice-president, Adriano Galliani, welcomed Balotelli's arrival, saying, "With his arrival, we have reinforced our team a lot. He's a dream come true, wanted by the [AC Milan president Silvio] Berlusconi and the club." Balotelli is expected to sign a four-and-a-half-year contract with Milan, subject to passing his medical. The move marks a new chapter in the striker's career, as he seeks to revive his form and achieve success with his new club.

New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady will miss the first four games of next season due to his involvement in the "Deflategate" scandal. The team has also been fined $1 million for their role in intentionally deflating footballs during an NFL semi-final game against the Indianapolis Colts in February. The controversy overshadowed the Super Bowl buildup, which the Patriots ultimately won. The punishment comes after an investigation found the team guilty of tampering with the balls to gain an unfair advantage. Brady's suspension and the fine are a significant penalty for the team's actions. The scandal sparked widespread debate.

A devastating explosion rocked the town of Khalis, located approximately 49 miles northeast of Baghdad, on Monday morning. According to a provincial official, the blast was "very strong" and has resulted in a significant loss of life. Hospital sources indicate that the death toll is expected to rise, with at least 20 people confirmed dead.

The explosion occurred at a checkpoint about two miles west of Khalis town centre, with a security source reporting that 22 people were also injured in the blast. A police officer at the scene confirmed that a suicide car bomber was responsible for the attack. The blast was so powerful that it set several vehicles ablaze, including a minibus packed with women and children.

This attack comes just a day after the Islamic State (IS) claimed responsibility for a suicide bomb attack on a security checkpoint in Baghdad, which killed at least 20 people. IS has been stepping up its suicide attacks in recent months, targeting predominantly Shia towns like Khalis. The militant group follows an extreme form of Sunni Islam and often targets Shia Muslims, whom it regards as apostates. The incident has sparked widespread concern, with officials warning of further attacks in the region.

A fatal six-car and motorbike collision occurred on the northbound carriageway in foggy conditions. Two women, Aneta Bula, 36, and Joan Kavanagh, 89, died from their injuries, with a coroner recording accidental death verdicts due to a head injury and multiple injuries, respectively.

A High Court judge has ruled against the family of murdered teacher Ann Maguire in their bid for a judicial review of the coroner's decision regarding her inquest. Ann Maguire, 61, was stabbed to death by her student Will Cornick at Corpus Christi Catholic College in Leeds in April 2014. The family had requested that the coroner call former pupils to give evidence, particularly those who had been interviewed by the police and had heard Cornick make threats on the day of the murder.

However, Mr Justice Holroyde dismissed the claim, stating that the assistant coroner's decision was not "so seriously flawed as to be unreasonable." He acknowledged the family's desire for a thorough examination of the circumstances surrounding Ann's death but ultimately agreed that calling former pupils to give evidence could cause them harm. The judge noted that the recorded police interviews with these students should be sufficient for the assistant coroner to consider.

Ann's widower, Don Maguire, expressed the family's disappointment but not surprise at the ruling. "We've been pulled backwards and forwards through the proverbial hedge quite a few times in the last few years," he said. Despite this setback, the family remains hopeful that someone will examine the full circumstances surrounding Ann's tragic murder and that proper lessons will be learned.

The inquest into Ann's death is scheduled to begin at Wakefield Coroners' Court in November. The Maguire family had wanted the coroner to investigate whether more could have been done to prevent the tragedy, particularly given that some students had heard Cornick's threats and claims of having knives in his bag on the day of the murder. However, others, including Ann's sisters and educators, had opposed the idea of questioning students, citing concerns about attaching blame and causing them undue distress.

One of Ann's sisters, Sheila Connor, a teacher herself, had expressed worry about the potential harm to students who might be questioned about their actions or lack of action before the killing. Dominic Kelly, vice-principal of Notre Dame Sixth Form College in Leeds, had also raised concerns, stating that some students had already expressed guilt and concern that they could have prevented the tragedy.

Will Cornick, who was 15 at the time of the murder, was given a life sentence in 2014 after admitting to Ann's murder. A report by Leeds Safeguarding Children Board in 2016 concluded that no one could have predicted or prevented Ann's murder. As the inquest approaches, the Maguire family and the community continue to seek answers and closure, while also hoping that lessons will be learned to prevent such tragedies from occurring in the future.

Sheffield United Patron Resigns Over Ched Evans Training Decision

In a shocking turn of events, Sheffield United's patron, Jessica Ennis-Hill's fellow ambassador, Ms. Webster, has resigned from her position in protest over the club's decision to allow former player Ched Evans to train with the team. The 25-year-old Welsh striker was released from prison last month after serving two-and-a-half years for raping a woman in a hotel room in Rhyl.

The club's decision to grant Evans permission to train with the side was made following a request from the Professional Footballers' Association. However, the move has sparked widespread controversy, with many criticizing the club for allowing a convicted rapist to return to the sport. Ms. Webster, who has been a vocal advocate for women's rights and has spoken publicly about her own experience of being sexually assaulted as a teenager, said that she could not continue in her role as patron while the club was considering re-signing Evans.

In an interview with BBC's Newsnight, Ms. Webster expressed her disappointment and frustration with the club's decision, stating that "at no point" had they acknowledged the "extremity of his crime." She also emphasized that Evans's return to the sport would have a significant impact on the community, particularly on young men who look up to him as a role model. "He's not just going into a job, he's bandied as a role model, we cheer him on as a role model and he's influencing the next generation of young men who are currently still making their decisions on how to treat women and what sexual mutual consent is," she said.

The club has stated that it has not yet made a decision on whether to re-sign Evans, but the fact that he has been allowed to train with the team has sparked outrage among many fans and campaign groups. A petition urging the club not to take Evans back has garnered nearly 157,000 signatures, and many have taken to social media to express their disapproval. Despite this, the club has maintained that it will not be swayed by "mob justice" and will consider the views of all stakeholders before making a decision.

Evans's case is due to be reviewed by the Criminal Cases Review Commission, and he maintains his innocence, claiming that the sex was consensual. However, his appeal against his conviction was rejected by three judges at the Court of Appeal in 2012. As the debate over Evans's return to football continues, Ms. Webster's resignation serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of considering the impact of such decisions on the community and on the victims of crime.

A Dhaka court has sentenced 13 members of the Awami League's student wing to life in prison for the brutal murder of Biswajit Das, a killing that sparked widespread outrage in Bangladesh. The incident, which was captured on live television, showed activists chasing and hacking Das to death with machetes in broad daylight. The prosecution stated that the attackers had mistaken Das for a supporter of the opposition party.

Only eight of the accused were present in court to hear the verdict, while the remaining five, including two who were sentenced to death, were tried in absentia as they remain at large. The victim's family has expressed satisfaction with the verdict, with Das's elder brother Uttam calling for the swift execution of the condemned men. "We have got the justice and now we want quick execution of these criminals," he said.

The trial has been seen as a major test for the ruling Awami League, which has faced allegations of attempting to cover up the identities of the attackers. The verdict comes amid a backdrop of street violence and protests ahead of the country's scheduled elections on January 5. The main opposition party, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has announced a boycott of the polls, citing concerns over the fairness of the electoral process. The opposition has demanded that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina step down to allow for a neutral caretaker government to oversee the elections.

Australia Dominates West Indies in Hobart Test

The Australian cricket team has taken a commanding lead over the West Indies in the ongoing Test match in Hobart. Adam Voges and Shaun Marsh stole the show with a record-breaking 449-run partnership for the fourth wicket, surpassing the previous record held by Bradman and Ponsford since 1934. Voges remained unbeaten on 269, while Marsh scored an impressive 182.

The Australian team declared their innings at 583-4, setting a daunting target for the West Indies. The visitors struggled to respond, losing six wickets for 116 runs at one stage. However, Darren Bravo's unbeaten 94 helped to stabilize the innings, and the West Indies ended the day at 207-6, still trailing by 376 runs.

Nathan Lyon was the pick of the Australian bowlers, taking three wickets to put pressure on the West Indies. Josh Hazlewood and Peter Siddle also chipped in with important wickets, while Steve Smith took a spectacular catch at slip to dismiss Rajindra Chandrika. The West Indies still require 177 runs to avoid the follow-on, and it will take a Herculean effort from their batsmen to save the match.

The day belonged to Voges and Marsh, who batted with ease and authority. Voges brought up his maiden Test double century from 285 balls, including 33 fours. The partnership between the two batsmen was a treat to watch, and it has put Australia in a strong position to win the match. With the West Indies facing an uphill task, it will be interesting to see how they respond on the next day.

Venezuela Braces for Sunday's Constituent Assembly Elections Amid Widespread Protests

Venezuela is on high alert as the country prepares for Sunday's elections to choose members of a constituent assembly, a move widely criticized by the opposition and international leaders. Despite calls to cancel the elections, President Nicolás Maduro remains resolute, claiming the assembly will promote peace and reconciliation by bringing together polarized sectors of society to discuss a new constitution.

However, critics argue that the assembly is a ploy by the president to expand his powers and entrench himself in office. The opposition has refused to participate in the elections, calling the assembly a tool for Maduro to consolidate his power. Opposition leader Leopoldo López, currently under house arrest, has urged Venezuelans to step up street protests, warning that the president's plan to rewrite the constitution will spell the end of the country's democracy.

López also appealed to the military to withdraw its support from the government, saying "I invite you to not be accomplices to the annihilation of the republic, to a constitutional fraud, to repression." The opposition fears that the constituent assembly will bypass the opposition-controlled legislature and potentially cancel elections for regional governors scheduled for December 10.

The government has dismissed international criticism, including from US President Donald Trump, EU foreign policy chief Federica Mogherini, and Organization of American States Secretary-General Luis Almagro, as meddling. Last week's demonstrations and 24-hour strike seem to have only hardened the government's resolve to proceed with the election.

As the country teeters on the brink of chaos, the opposition remains confident that it can shutdown most of the country until Friday, when a massive demonstration is scheduled in the capital, Caracas. The protests have already resulted in over 100 deaths since they began on April 1, and tensions are expected to escalate in the coming days. With the international community watching, Venezuela stands at a critical juncture, as its citizens fight for their democratic rights and the future of their country.

NHS Misses Waiting Time Target as Patient Numbers Continue to Rise

The latest NHS England statistics have revealed that the health service has narrowly missed its target of treating 92% of patients within 18 weeks of their referral. As of the end of December, 91.8% of patients on the waiting list had been waiting less than 18 weeks, falling just short of the target that was put in place in April 2012.

Despite this, hospitals continue to treat more than nine out of 10 patients within the 18-week timeframe, with over 1.14 million patients starting consultant-led treatment in December alone. The total number of patients referred in 2015 was also up 4.1% on the previous year, highlighting the increasing demand on the NHS.

However, the number of patients waiting to start treatment for routine operations has risen to just under 3.3 million, with 755 people having waited for longer than 52 weeks. The Royal College of Surgeons has expressed concern over the rising number of delays, particularly for operations such as hip and knee replacements.

The president of the Royal College of Surgeons, Clare Marx, said: "Delayed treatment is extremely distressing to all patients. It is welcome that the government has promised extra money in the comprehensive spending review, but we also need a long-term sustainable plan to address the increasing numbers of patients needing surgery."

The NHS England figures also show a rise in the number of days patients were delayed from leaving hospital or other care settings. This has led to concerns that hospitals are being forced to cancel operations due to a lack of available beds. Marx warned that this not only places patients at greater safety risk but also denies much-needed hospital beds to others.

The NHS has been under significant pressure in recent months, with the first junior doctors' strike scheduled to take place on December 1, although it was called off at the last minute. Despite this, hospitals had already cancelled a few thousand operations, highlighting the challenges faced by the health service. As the NHS continues to struggle with rising patient numbers and increasing demand, it remains to be seen how it will cope with the ongoing pressure.

Ivory Coast's Government Dissolved Amidst Political Tensions

In a surprise move, Ivory Coast's President Alassane Ouattara has dissolved the government, citing a breakdown in relations with his coalition partners. The decision comes after the Democratic Party of Côte d'Ivoire (PDCI), a key member of the ruling coalition, voted against a new marriage law proposed by Mr. Ouattara's party, the Rally of the Republicans (RDR).

The proposed law aimed to recognize women as equal heads of household, challenging the current law that grants husbands sole decision-making authority. While the RDR supported the changes, the PDCI and other coalition members opposed them, highlighting the deepening rifts within the government.

The PDCI, which governed Ivory Coast for 39 years until a 1999 coup, had backed Mr. Ouattara in the disputed 2010 presidential election. In return, Mr. Ouattara appointed a prime minister from the PDCI. However, sources suggest that Mr. Ouattara feels the PDCI no longer fully supports him, prompting the dissolution of the government.

The move has sparked concerns about the country's continued political instability, which has plagued Ivory Coast since the 2010 election. The election sparked months of unrest, resulting in over 3,000 deaths, before former President Laurent Gbagbo was forced from office with the help of French and UN troops.

Despite presiding over an economic recovery since assuming control in 2011, Mr. Ouattara's government has faced numerous challenges, including armed attacks on military targets and infrastructure, allegedly launched by Gbagbo's allies from neighboring Ghana. The border between the two countries was closed for two weeks in September following an attack on an army checkpoint.

The dissolution of the government has raised questions about Mr. Ouattara's commitment to national reconciliation, with critics accusing him of not doing enough to promote unity between his supporters and those of Gbagbo, who is currently awaiting trial for crimes against humanity at the International Criminal Court in The Hague. As Ivory Coast, the world's largest cocoa producer, navigates this uncertain period, analysts warn that the country's fragile stability is at risk of being further undermined.

New Standards Commissioner Appointed to Oversee MP Conduct

The government has announced the appointment of Kathryn Stone as the new Parliamentary Standards Commissioner. She will take on the role of overseeing the code of conduct and rules for MPs, including the register of financial interests, starting in January. Ms Stone has a wealth of experience, having served as the commissioner for victims and survivors of the Troubles in Northern Ireland and currently holding the position of chief legal ombudsman of England and Wales. She has also worked with the Independent Police Complaints Commission and spent 11 years as chief executive of the charity Voice UK. Ms Stone will replace Kathryn Hudson in the position. Her appointment aims to bring transparency and accountability to the parliamentary standards process. With her extensive background in public service, Ms Stone is well-equipped to take on this critical role.

South East Asia on High Alert as IS Influence Grows

The recent attack on Jakarta in January has proven that the warnings issued by Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore in 2015 were sadly prophetic. The region's authorities have learned from past experiences, including the 2002 Bali bombings carried out by Jemaah Islamiyah (JI) militants inspired by Al Qaeda. However, the growing influence of the Islamic State (IS) in the region has raised concerns about the potential for more large-scale attacks.

IS has become a new draw for would-be jihadists across South East Asia, with several militant groups pledging allegiance to the group. It is estimated that up to 1,000 people from Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines have traveled to Syria and Iraq to fight with IS. The formation of an official wing of the group, known as Katibah Nusantara Daulah Islamiyah, comprising Indonesian and Malay speakers, has further heightened concerns. Security experts believe that the leaders of this wing are attempting to fund and encourage attacks across the region.

Over the past year, IS has increased its propaganda efforts in Indonesian, which is similar to Malay, inciting people to join the group and carry out attacks in their home countries. The Jakarta attack, initially thought to have been directed by an Indonesian militant in Syria, is now believed to have been organized by a local group called Jamaah Anshar Khilifah. The authorities are also on the lookout for foreign militants who may travel to the region to share or acquire battlefield knowledge.

The region's long coastlines and porous borders make it challenging for authorities to monitor and prevent the movement of militants. In recent months, the Philippine army has killed two Malaysians fighting with Abu Sayyaf in the south, while Indonesian authorities have arrested four Uighurs from China over links to the Mujahidin Indonesia Timur (MIT) group in Sulawesi. Additionally, two Uighurs were killed while fighting with MIT, and militants from Syria, Iraq, and Turkey have been sighted in the region, with some arrested over planned attacks.

Security experts warn that the competition to lead a potential official IS regional province may spur further attacks. Although IS has acknowledged pledges from some groups in the region, it has not yet formally declared the region a "province." However, there are signs that the group is moving towards doing so, which could have significant implications for the region's security.

The authorities in South East Asia are taking the threat seriously and are working to prevent further attacks. However, the region's complex geography and the growing influence of IS make it a challenging task. As the threat from IS continues to evolve, the region's governments must remain vigilant and work together to prevent the spread of extremism and violence. With the memory of the Jakarta attack still fresh, the region is on high alert, and the authorities are bracing themselves for the possibility of more attacks in the future.

A German restaurant owner has taken a bold stance against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan by selling burgers garnished with goat's cheese, dubbed the "Erdogan-Burger." Joerg Tiemann, the owner of Urban Burgery, claims the dish is a "satirical answer" to Erdogan's reaction to a German comic's poem that poked fun at him. The poem, read by Jan Boehmermann on German TV, referenced sex with goats and sheep, prompting Erdogan to file a criminal complaint against the comic.

The Erdogan-Burger has become a surprise hit, accounting for 75% of the restaurant's turnover. Tiemann describes it as a "classic hamburger, meat or vegetarian, with a thick slice of goat's cheese." He plans to continue selling the dish "for as long as people want it or until Erdogan ends his policy." Tiemann's protest is also a show of solidarity with two Turkish journalists, Erdem Gul and Can Dundar, who were jailed for reporting on Turkey's alleged arms shipments to Syrian rebels.

However, the restaurant has faced threats, mostly in the form of comments on Facebook, with some individuals warning that they would send the Grey Wolves, a Turkish nationalist group, to the restaurant. In response, Tiemann has installed eight 24-hour surveillance cameras and has received visits from German national security agents. Three Turkish workers left the restaurant due to the threats, but Tiemann has found alternative staff with the help of friends.

The controversy surrounding the Erdogan-Burger is part of a larger debate in Germany over freedom of speech. German prosecutors are investigating whether Boehmermann broke a law against insulting foreign leaders, prompting concerns about the limits of satire and criticism. Tiemann's restaurant has become a symbol of resistance against Erdogan's crackdown on dissent, which has drawn international criticism. As the Urban Burgery reopens, it remains to be seen how long the Erdogan-Burger will remain on the menu, but for now, it continues to be a popular choice among customers.

Government Announces £415m Funding for Schools to Promote Healthier Lifestyles

The government has announced that every school in the country will receive a share of £415m in funding to promote healthier lifestyles among students. The funding, which comes from the soft drinks industry levy, will be used to improve facilities for physical exercise and mental health. Education Secretary Justine Greening stated that the investment will have long-lasting benefits for children, saying "the health and wellbeing benefits can last a lifetime."

The soft drinks industry levy, introduced in last year's Budget, aims to tackle childhood obesity by applying a tax on sugary drinks. The government expects the levy to raise £520m in 2018-19, with the majority being allocated to schools. However, the funding will only be used for capital projects, such as improving sports facilities and promoting healthy eating, and will not be used to pay for staff, including PE teachers.

All state-funded primary and secondary schools, as well as sixth forms, will receive a portion of the funding. Additionally, schools will be able to bid for funding for specific projects. Greening emphasized the importance of schools in promoting healthy lifestyles, saying "schools can really help our children get a healthy start in life from exercise and sport, and also from knowing what a healthy diet means."

However, the British Soft Drinks Association has criticized the levy, saying it is "odd to hinge this investment on a punitive tax" against the industry, which has already made significant reductions in sugar content. Director General Gavin Partington argued that there is no evidence to suggest that the tax will reduce obesity levels. Despite this, the government remains committed to using the levy to promote healthier lifestyles among children.

Tragedy struck at the T in the Park music festival in Perthshire, Scotland, as two teenagers were found dead on the festival grounds. According to Police Scotland, the deaths of the 17-year-old male from the west of Scotland and the 17-year-old female from the north of England are not thought to be suspicious, but investigations are ongoing to determine the exact circumstances.

The festival, which is being attended by over 80,000 people, has been marred by the tragic loss of the two young lives. Festival organisers expressed their shock and sadness at the news, with director Geoff Ellis stating, "We are shocked and saddened by today's news and our thoughts are with the families and friends at this time." The organisers are offering their full support and assistance to the affected families.

Police are exploring various lines of inquiry, including the possibility that the deaths may be drug-related. Event commander Chief Superintendent Angela McLaren warned festival-goers that "there is no safe way of taking drugs" and urged them to be cautious. In response, the festival organisers took to Twitter to encourage anyone with drugs to dispose of them in special bins, assuring that those who do so will not face any trouble.

This is not the first time that the festival has been affected by tragic incidents. In previous years, there have been deaths at the festival, including a 36-year-old man who was found dead in the toilets in 2015 and a 24-year-old man who collapsed and died during the night in 2010.

Despite the tragedy, the festival is continuing, with revised travel and campsite plans in place to avoid a repeat of last year's traffic problems. Organisers have implemented colour-coded zones, better signage, and 24-hour dedicated management teams to ensure a smoother experience for attendees. However, police are also investigating the theft of a cash machine from the main arena area, which contained a significant amount of cash. The incident occurred sometime between midnight and 7:00 am on Friday, and officers are appealing for information.

BBC Launches WhatsApp Service to Combat Ebola Spread

In an effort to provide critical public health information and combat the spread of Ebola in West Africa, the BBC has launched a WhatsApp service.
