Notts County and Arsenal played to a thrilling 1-1 draw in front of a crowd of 1,583 at Meadow Lane, with both teams creating numerous scoring opportunities. The hosts took the lead in the 27th minute courtesy of a cool finish from Jess Clarke, who sidestepped two defenders before slotting the ball into the far corner of the net. Clarke, playing up front in the absence of Ellen White, had gone close with a couple of early long-range efforts and her goal was well-deserved.

However, Arsenal came out strong in the second half, with Japanese midfielder Yukari Kinga having a header well saved by keeper Carly Telford in the 49th minute. Just four minutes later, the Gunners leveled the score when right-back Alex Scott drilled an 18-yard volley into the far corner of the net. Arsenal continued to push for a winner, with striker Kelly Smith being desperately unlucky not to give her team the lead as her 72nd-minute free-kick hit the bar and bounced clear off the goal line.

Substitute Freda Ayisi also had a chance to win the game for Arsenal, but her 12-yard shot was headed off the line by central defender Sophie Bradley. Despite their improved second-half display, the Gunners were unable to force a winner, but will be boosted by their performance ahead of their upcoming fixtures.

In the night's other game, Birmingham City fought out a 0-0 draw with Everton at their new Solihull ground in front of 657 fans. The match was a tightly contested affair, with both teams creating scoring opportunities but neither able to find the back of the net. Everton striker Nikita Parris had an early header saved by goalkeeper Rebecca Spencer, while Birmingham's Katie Wilkinson had a shot fly over the bar in the 29th minute.

The Toffees continued to look the sharper side in front of goal, with Danielle Turner striking the post and Billie Murphy having a close-range shot saved by Spencer. However, Birmingham almost took the lead eight minutes from time, with Kirsty Linnett driving in a 30-yard shot that hit the bar. The draw will be a welcome point for Birmingham, who face a tough Champions League semi-final against Swedish team Tyreso in just three days' time.

European Athletics Launches Review of Records Amid Doping Scandals

In the wake of growing concerns over doping in athletics, European Athletics (EA) president Svein Arne Hansen has ordered a review of European records to ensure they are "100% believable and credible". The move comes as Russian athletes face a ban from competing due to a state-sponsored doping program, and Olympic legend Usain Bolt is set to lose a gold medal after a teammate tested positive for banned substances.

The review, which will report back its findings by September, aims to scrutinize the legitimacy of European records, particularly those held by Russian athletes. Currently, the EA website lists 15 European indoor and outdoor athletics records held by Russians, as well as additional records set in the 1980s by athletes from Soviet Bloc countries, including East Germany, which operated its own extensive doping program.

Hansen emphasized the importance of records being respected and recognized as beyond question by athletes and fans. "Claiming a European record - after being crowned European Champion - is the pinnacle of our sport in Europe. The holders of these records should be aspirational heroes whose performances are respected and recognised as beyond question by their fellow athletes and the fans of our sport," he said.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is also taking action, re-testing hundreds of samples from the 2008 and 2012 Olympic Games using up-to-date detection methods. So far, almost 100 athletes have been sanctioned for using banned substances, including Jamaican sprinter Nesta Carter, who was part of the Jamaican quartet that won the 4x100m relay in Beijing in 2008, featuring Usain Bolt. As a result, Jamaica will be stripped of its medal.

Hansen has spoken with Lord Coe, head of the IAAF, athletics' world governing body, about the review, and the IAAF will monitor the work closely before deciding on any actions at the world level. The review is a significant step towards restoring integrity and trust in athletics, and ensuring that European records are a true reflection of athletic achievement.

Tragedy struck in Quinta do Conde, a town 30km south of Lisbon, as a dispute over a barking dog turned deadly. A 77-year-old man allegedly opened fire after a row with a neighbor, sparking a chaotic sequence of events. A plainclothes officer, who lived in the area, was fatally shot while investigating the disturbance. A patrol officer responding to the scene was also shot in the head and killed. The officer's son, who attempted to aid his father, was seriously injured in the crossfire and later succumbed to his wounds in hospital. The gunman, who reportedly tried to take his own life with a hunting rifle, was arrested and hospitalized. Neighbors expressed shock, stating that while the man had previously threatened to harm someone over the barking dog, they never thought he would act on it.

Nottingham Forest Chairman Fawaz Al Hasawi has expressed his excitement as manager Billy Davies returns to the club on a three-and-a-half year deal. Davies, 49, previously managed Forest from 2009 to 2011, leading the team to consecutive play-off campaigns. After being sacked in 2011, he has now returned to the City Ground, becoming the fourth manager to work under the Al Hasawi ownership in seven months. Last season, Forest narrowly missed the Championship play-offs, but currently sit fourth in the table after 11 games. Davies' return has brought optimism to the club, with Al Hasawi looking forward to working with him to bring success back to Nottingham Forest. With Davies at the helm, the team aims to build on their strong start to the season and push for promotion.

Labour Pledges to Protect EU Funding for Deprived Regions

In a significant commitment, the Labour Party has vowed to safeguard the funding of deprived regions in the UK that currently receive financial support from the European Union. Shadow Foreign Secretary Emily Thornberry announced at the party's conference in Liverpool that a future Labour government would guarantee to make up any shortfall in structural funding into the 2020s and beyond.

The move is seen as a key plank of Labour's next manifesto, with Ms Thornberry emphasizing that the communities most affected by Brexit must be protected. She criticized the government's current offer, which guarantees EU-funded projects signed before the Autumn statement and agricultural funding until 2020, as "hedged in conditions" and lacking long-term certainty.

Without a clear guarantee of funding, Ms Thornberry argued that the most deprived regions and communities cannot plan ahead, attract investment, or make progress. She pledged that Labour would fill any funding gap, with regions such as Wales, south west England, and the North West set to benefit. Wales is currently allocated £2.1bn, south west England £1.3bn, and the North West £979m under the current seven-year programme.

Ms Thornberry also used her speech to praise Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, who was re-elected on Saturday, and to attack the government's handling of Brexit. She accused the government of having "no plan" for the UK's exit from the EU and promised that Labour would "stand up" for EU migrants, UK businesses, and workers' rights.

Labour has committed to opposing any attempts by the government to scrap legal rights and funding programmes derived from Britain's EU membership. The party will publish a document outlining the full range of benefits that are under threat, with regional funding being a key area of concern. By establishing a domestic fund for less prosperous regions, Labour aims to protect the level of funding currently received from the EU, using the estimated net savings from Britain's withdrawal to prioritize this commitment.

The pledge has been welcomed by delegates at the Labour conference, who see it as a vital step in protecting the most vulnerable communities from the impact of Brexit. With the government's Brexit plan still unclear, Labour's commitment to safeguarding EU funding is likely to be a major issue in the run-up to the next general election.

A Call to Ban Hot Food on the London Tube

Lord Sherbourne has sparked a debate in the House of Lords by suggesting that hot food should be banned on the London Tube network. He argued that the consumption of hot food on trains is "very offensive" to many passengers and creates litter that can pose a health hazard. The peer pointed out that smoking and alcohol are already prohibited on the network and questioned why hot food should be treated differently.

Lord Sherbourne cited cities like Washington DC, which have implemented similar bans, as examples that London could follow. He urged Transport Minister Lord Ahmad to raise the matter with Transport for London (TfL) and consider conducting a passenger survey to gauge public opinion on the issue.

In response, Lord Ahmad acknowledged the concern but stated that there are currently "no plans" to introduce a ban on hot food on the Tube. However, he promised to discuss the matter with TfL and noted that the transport authority already has a policy in place to promote good travel etiquette among passengers. While a ban may not be on the horizon, the debate highlights the ongoing efforts to improve the commuting experience for Londoners. The issue is likely to continue to be a topic of discussion among transport officials and passengers alike.

Environment Secretary Enjoys Warm Welcome and Local Fare at Gloucester Services

In a lighthearted moment during a recent Parliamentary debate, Environment Secretary Liz Truss was invited to visit Gloucester Services, a renowned motorway stop-off, and enjoy a traditional Gloucester Old Spot sausage. The offer, extended by Gloucester MP Richard Graham, was met with laughter in the Commons, but Ms Truss took him up on it, visiting the services on Friday.

Upon arrival, she was treated to a cooked breakfast, complete with a locally-sourced sausage, which she proclaimed "very nice". The sausage, made from Gloucestershire Old Spot meat, was a highlight of her meal, with Ms Truss praising its "really lovely" flavor and the passion of the local producers who made it.

Gloucester Services has gained a reputation for defying the typical motorway services stereotype, instead offering upmarket, organic fare from local suppliers. The site, which features independent shops and restaurants, sources produce from 130 local suppliers within a 30-mile radius. Ms Truss praised the services as "a brilliant example of promoting local food" and highlighted its role in bringing together local producers to create an exceptional experience for visitors.

The visit comes as part of the government's efforts to promote British food, following the launch of the Great British Food Unit in November. The unit aims to help Britain become a "great food nation" by bringing together "food and drink pioneers" to support the industry. With its commitment to local, high-quality produce, Gloucester Services is a shining example of this initiative in action.

Concerns Over Pencil Use in Voting Prompt Calls for Change

The use of pencils to mark ballot papers in the recent EU referendum has sparked widespread concern among voters, with many taking to social media to express their fears that votes could be altered. The issue has prompted the Electoral Commission to receive almost 200 calls from worried voters, and has led to calls for the government to provide alternative writing instruments.

Lib Dem Lord Rennard has asked the government to consider providing "special ballot pens" instead of pencils, citing concerns that pencil marks could be easily erased and changed. The Electoral Commission has stated that it is looking into "alternatives to providing pencils for voters in polling stations which could improve confidence" in the voting process.

The controversy surrounding pencil use in voting began on social media, where the hashtag #usepens gained traction on Twitter. Many voters expressed concerns that ballot papers filled out in pencil could be rubbed out and changed, potentially altering the outcome of the referendum. In response, the Electoral Commission has noted that voters are able to use either a pen or pencil to mark their ballot paper, and that there is no law requiring the use of one over the other.

Despite this, the Commission has acknowledged that the use of pencils may not be the most secure or reliable method of voting. Historically, pencils have been used for practical reasons, as pens can dry out or spill, causing problems with the voting process. However, the Commission is now working with returning officers and national governments to explore alternative options that could improve voter confidence.

A Cabinet Office spokeswoman, Baroness Chisholm of Owlpen, has stated that the government is aware of the concerns surrounding pencil use, but has noted that there were no reported cases of ballot papers being changed during the referendum. The Electoral Commission's report into the EU referendum has highlighted the need for alternative voting methods, and it is likely that changes will be made to the voting process in the future to address the concerns of voters.

Russell Knox has maintained his position at the top of the leaderboard at the World Golf Championships in Shanghai, matching Hideki Matsuyama's impressive four-under round of 68. The Scottish golfer now stands at 14 under par, tied with Matsuyama for the lead. American Daniel Berger is close behind, just one shot off the pace, while Bill Haas and Francesco Molinari are a further stroke back on 12 under.

Rory McIlroy, the world number three, had a mixed day, carding an up-and-down 70 at Sheshan International. He showed glimpses of brilliance, including a remarkable recovery shot on the eighth hole, but was ultimately hindered by bogeys on the 11th, 12th, and 15th. Despite picking up strokes on the 16th and 18th, McIlroy finds himself eight shots off the lead.

Knox, who is bidding to become the second player to retain a World Golf Championships title, came agonizingly close to a hole-in-one on the fourth hole. He then applied pressure on Matsuyama with a shot on the 13th, but found water on the 14th. However, the 31-year-old showed remarkable resilience, holing from 25 feet for an unlikely par before birdying the 15th.

As the tournament enters its final stages, Matsuyama is poised to make history as the first Japanese player to win a WGC event. Meanwhile, Ross Fisher and Shane Lowry have made notable moves up the leaderboard, with Fisher tied for sixth on 10 under and Lowry joining McIlroy and Henrik Stenson on nine under. In contrast, Danny Willett endured another difficult day, carding a 75 to leave him 11 over par.

Revolutionary Changes Proposed for Rugby League Structure

The Rugby Football League (RFL) has unveiled three groundbreaking proposals to transform the sport's competitive structure, with the aim of introducing positive change and innovation across the entire sport. The proposed changes, which cannot be implemented until the start of the 2015 season, have been met with enthusiasm from clubs and fans alike. RFL chief executive Nigel Wood expressed his optimism, stating, "The interest already shown in these ideas has been very encouraging, and I believe these new proposals will produce positive change and innovation across the whole sport."

The current licensing system, which has been in place since 2009, has granted 14 clubs three-year licenses, making them immune to relegation. However, this system has been met with criticism from some clubs, particularly those in the Championship, who are advocating for a return to regular promotion and relegation. In response to these concerns, the RFL has consulted with all Super League and Championship clubs, and a proposal to maintain the status quo was rejected.

The three proposed options aim to address the concerns of clubs and fans while ensuring the long-term sustainability of the sport. Option 1 suggests a 12-team Super League competition, with a 10 or 12-team Championship, and one club promoted and relegated each year. Option 2 proposes a two-division Super League, with each division comprising 10 teams. The most radical proposal, Option 3, involves two divisions of 12 teams in Super League, with teams playing each other once before splitting into three groups of eight in mid-season and then playing each other home and away.

The third option would culminate in a play-off series and a Grand Final or play-off final, with the final standings determining the makeup of the two 12-team divisions for the following season. This option would result in two teams being relegated from Super League at the end of next season. Wood emphasized the need for a balanced approach, stating, "I do believe that we need to create a pathway into Super League, but it is essential that we are mindful of the challenges that a straight reintroduction of promotion and relegation between part-time and full-time leagues would create."

The RFL has sought the expertise of sports industry financial experts KPMG in drafting its proposals, ensuring that the changes are well-researched and sustainable. Wood acknowledged the progress made in recent years and the need to avoid destabilizing the sport. "While there is a recognition that the time is right for change, we fully understand the need to avoid destabilizing the excellent progress that has been made in recent years," he said.

The proposed changes have sparked excitement and debate among fans and clubs, with many welcoming the potential for innovation and positive change. As the RFL continues to consult with stakeholders, it is clear that the future of rugby league is set to undergo a significant transformation. With the introduction of these new proposals, the sport is poised to enter a new era of competitiveness, excitement, and growth.

England wicketkeeper Jonny Bairstow led a stunning Yorkshire fightback on the opening day of their County Championship match against Durham at Chester-le-Street. Bairstow hit a magnificent 102 and shared an unbroken seventh-wicket stand of 138 with Tim Bresnan as the visitors closed on 329-6.

Yorkshire's batsmen all reached double figures, but it was Bairstow and Bresnan (66 not out) who stole the show. Bairstow's 126-ball innings, which included 16 fours, turned the day on its head after Yorkshire had been struggling on 191-6. Bresnan's equally attacking knock, off just 85 balls, was just as crucial and took his Championship batting average past 65 for the season.

Earlier, Durham had won the toss and decided to bowl first under overcast skies. Alex Lees and Will Rhodes played watchfully to see out the majority of the morning session with an opening stand of 56. However, when Rhodes was bowled by Jamie Harrison, who was making his return after 13 months out following a knee operation, wickets began to fall at regular intervals.

Yorkshire looked in danger of being bowled out for less than 250 when Adil Rashid became the sixth wicket to fall. But Bairstow and Bresnan's attack on a tiring Durham bowling unit put their side firmly on top and in with a chance of gaining maximum batting points.

Bairstow was delighted with his own innings, saying: "The way the openers applied themselves was fantastic. It was highly skilful. It set us up and you always know that one session here can change the game." He added: "I'm delighted with my own innings. I enjoy playing here - we had a lot of our own supporters here and the Durham fans gave me a good reception."

Durham's Jamie Harrison, who took 2-62 on his return to first-team action, was happy to be back playing after a long injury layoff. "I'm just happy to be playing," he said. "I've had four years of struggling with injuries and it's been really tough." Yorkshire will be looking to build on their strong start and score as many runs as possible to put pressure on Durham. With Bairstow and Bresnan still at the crease, they will be confident of achieving their goal.

A court in Jhelum has rejected the bail application of Chaudhry Muhammad Shakeel, accused of murdering his ex-wife Samia Shahid. The 28-year-old beautician from Bradford died in July while visiting relatives in Pakistan. Her second husband, Syed Mukhtar Kazam, claims she was killed because her family disapproved of their marriage. Initially, it was reported that Ms Shahid had died of a heart attack, but a post-mortem examination revealed she had been strangled. Ms Shahid's father, Chaudhry Muhammad Shahid, was held as a suspected accessory but has been released on bail. Mr Kazam is seeking to have the case moved, citing threats to his life from Ms Shahid's family. The Lahore High Court is set to hear his application. The Jhelum court has indicated that a higher court may yet consider Mr Shakeel's bail request.

Sue Beatt has been elected as the new Chair of Bowls Scotland, following the retirement of Bill Knox. Beatt, a passionate bowler from Glasgow, has been a director of the organization for two and a half years. She has pledged to sustain the sport for future generations while supporting current members and clubs. Beatt brings a wealth of business experience to the role, as the owner and director of People Solutions (Scotland) Ltd and The Whisky Ambassador Limited. Outgoing chair Bill Knox welcomed Beatt's election, stating that she has the relevant skills for the position and will be a great asset to the board. Beatt expressed her pride at being elected and is committed to working tirelessly for the benefit of the sport. Her appointment has been warmly received by the bowling community.

The Outer Hebrides population has declined to 27,070, according to the latest figures released in June last year. This represents a decrease of 180 people since 2014. In an effort to address this issue, the local authority, Comhairle nan Eilean Siar, is set to develop a framework for a policy to tackle population decline at an upcoming seminar.

Islands Minister Humza Yousaf has been invited to attend the event, which is scheduled to take place in the autumn. Councillor Angus Campbell emphasized the importance of attracting people to the islands, stating that positive net migration is crucial to counteracting the negative natural change that the Outer Hebrides is experiencing.

The islands offer a good quality of life, but Councillor Campbell noted that providing infrastructure, including good and affordable housing, services, and a multi-agency approach, is essential to fulfilling people's aspirations. Depopulation has long been a concern for the Western Isles, with research suggesting that more women than men are leaving the islands. The Hebrides Migration Study found a long-term decline in population between 1901 and 2001, with the steepest decline in Harris, the Uists, and Barra. The comhairle is working to address this issue and develop a policy to reverse the decline and ensure a sustainable future for the Outer Hebrides.

Violence Erupts at Trump Rallies, Critics Accuse Him of Encouraging Hate

The presidential campaign of Donald Trump has been marred by violent clashes between his supporters and protesters, with critics accusing him of encouraging hate and division. The latest incident occurred on Friday in Chicago, where a rally was forced to be called off due to violent clashes between supporters and protesters. The clashes, which took place at the University of Illinois at Chicago, resulted in several injuries and arrests.

Democratic candidate Bernie Sanders has been vocal in his criticism of Trump, calling him a "pathological liar" and accusing him of conducting a cynical campaign of hate and fear. Sanders also urged Trump to tell his supporters that violence is not acceptable in the political process. Fellow Democratic candidate Hillary Clinton has also weighed in, accusing Trump of encouraging his supporters to beat up protesters and then offering to pay their legal costs.

The controversy surrounding Trump's rallies has been building for some time. On Saturday, a man tried to rush the stage as Trump spoke in Ohio, but was stopped by Secret Service agents. Additionally, a Trump supporter was charged with assault after punching a protester at a rally in North Carolina, with Trump later saying that the supporter's actions were "appropriate". Trump's campaign manager, Corey Lewandowski, has also been accused of assaulting a female journalist, Michelle Fields of Breitbart, although he denies the accusation.

As the Republican primaries approach, with votes taking place in states including Florida and Ohio on Tuesday, Trump's rivals are seizing on the controversy surrounding his rallies. Marco Rubio, currently in third place, has said that a win in his home state of Florida is vital to prevent the Republican nomination from being "hijacked" by Trump. With the campaign season heating up, it remains to be seen how the controversy surrounding Trump's rallies will impact his chances of securing the nomination.

Despite the criticism, Trump has denied using hate speech or playing any part in fostering division. However, his rivals and critics argue that his rhetoric and actions have created a toxic atmosphere that encourages violence and intolerance. As the presidential campaign continues, it is clear that the issue of violence at Trump rallies will remain a contentious and divisive issue. With tensions running high, it remains to be seen how the situation will unfold in the coming days and weeks.

Dennis Kimetto made history yesterday by becoming the first man to run a marathon in under two hours and three minutes. The 30-year-old Kenyan achieved this incredible feat at the Berlin Marathon, finishing with a time of 2:02:57. Kimetto shook off fellow Kenyan Emmanuel Mutai with just under three miles remaining, securing his victory and breaking the previous world record.

Mutai, who finished second with a time of 2:03:13, also broke the previous record set by Wilson Kipsang last year. Kimetto had promised to attack the record if conditions allowed, and the perfect weather in Berlin enabled him to keep his promise. The lead group stayed together throughout the race, with Kimetto sprinting to victory in the final stretch.

Mutai believes that a two-hour marathon is possible, saying "times are coming down and down. So if not today, then tomorrow." Kimetto's win marks a significant milestone in long-distance running, and his achievement is likely to inspire other athletes to push the boundaries of human endurance. In other results, Scott Overall finished 14th in the men's race with a time of 2:13:00, while Britain's Shelly Woods won the women's wheelchair race.

England's women's team has risen to second in the world rankings. They finished third at the World Cup last year. The team recently came third at the SheBelieves Cup, and will host Belgium on April 8 in Euro 2017 qualifiers, having won their first two games. USA remains top of the rankings, with Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland also placing.

Rosneft, Russia's largest oil producer, has reported a significant decline in net income for the third quarter, with profits reaching 26bn roubles ($400.7m; £318m). This figure is substantially lower than expected, reflecting the challenging environment in the commodity markets. The company's chief executive, Igor Sechin, cited the difficulties in the sector, which have been exacerbated by low crude prices.

The news comes as the Russian government, which owns approximately three-quarters of Rosneft, prepares to sell a 20% stake in the company as part of a privatisation programme. The sale is expected to raise £9bn for the cash-strapped government, which has been impacted by the decline in commodity prices. UK oil giant BP, which owns 20% of Rosneft, has also been affected by the sector's struggles, recently reporting a near-halving of its third-quarter profits.

The decline in oil prices, which peaked at $115 a barrel in 2014, has had a significant impact on the industry, with many major oil companies reporting lower profits. Despite a recent surge in prices following Opec's agreement to limit production, doubts over the cartel's ability to deliver cuts have seen prices slip, with Brent crude currently trading at $45.77 a barrel. The challenging market conditions are likely to continue, with Rosneft and other oil producers facing ongoing uncertainty.

The pressure to succeed in exams is taking a toll on an increasing number of young people, according to a leading children's charity. Data from ChildLine, a helpline run by the NSPCC, reveals that the charity conducted 3,077 counselling sessions about exam-related stress over the past year, a 9% increase on the previous year.

The helpline also reported a significant rise in the number of counselling sessions about exam results, with 1,127 sessions taking place, a 20% increase on 2014/15. The charity says that the pressure to do well is being felt by a growing number of young people across the country, with many struggling to cope with the stress and anxiety of exams.

One 15-year-old boy who contacted ChildLine said: "All I can think about is exams and I just can't deal with it anymore. I'm revising all night because I'm so worried I'll fail, and I feel so tired all the time." A 17-year-old girl also admitted: "I feel so overwhelmed at the moment, it's impossible to concentrate on revising. I'm worried that I won't get the grade I'm predicted, and I don't know where to start."

NSPCC chief executive Peter Wanless said: "The exam period can be a very stressful and anxious time for young people. We hear from lots of young people each year who are anxious, worried, or panicking about their exams and revision." To help young people cope with exam stress, ChildLine has launched a new video offering tips and advice, including taking regular breaks from revising, exercising, getting a good night's sleep, and thinking positively.

The charity is also advising parents and carers to avoid placing unnecessary pressure on children to achieve certain grades, and to help them revise by giving them time and space to do so. Young people can call ChildLine free on 0800 11 11 for confidential advice and support. As the exam season approaches, the charity is urging young people to reach out for help if they're feeling overwhelmed, and reminding them that they're not alone in their concerns.

The BBC's Spotlight programme has won a prestigious Royal Television Society Journalism Award. The award recognizes the team's investigative journalism in exposing secret dealings behind Northern Ireland's biggest property deal in 2014, involving Nama. Secret recordings uncovered by reporter Mandy McAuley revealed hidden transactions. The programme team received the RTS Nations and Regions Current Affairs award in London. BBC Northern Ireland's Director, Peter Johnston, praised the team's dedication to producing high-quality journalism, continuing Spotlight's tradition of award-winning programmes. The award acknowledges the team's hard-hitting investigative work.

Bradford City is set to sign Blackpool's club captain, Colin Doyle. The 31-year-old goalkeeper will undergo a medical early next week. Doyle was a standout performer in League One last season despite Blackpool's relegation. He will join Nicky Law and Nathaniel Knight-Percival as summer recruits. With Ben Williams' departure to Bury, Doyle is likely to become the Bantams' number one. His release clause allowed him to explore options after Blackpool's relegation. The move is expected to be completed soon, ahead of Bradford's season opener against Port Vale on August 6.

The pound experienced a significant surge after a recent survey revealed a strong rebound in manufacturing activity for August. It rose 1% to $1.327 and nearly 1% against the euro at €1.187. The Purchasing Managers' Index jumped to a 10-month high, attributed to the pound's post-Brexit weakness boosting exports. However, this also increased costs for companies. On the stock market, housebuilders saw gains, with Berkeley Group, Taylor Wimpey, and Persimmon rising. In contrast, Vodafone, GlaxoSmithKline, and Shell saw declines of 2-3%. The pound's rebound is a positive sign for the UK's economic recovery.

Guinea is set to hold its presidential election, with seven candidates challenging incumbent President Alpha Conde. Conde's main opponent, Cellou Dalein Diallo, has urged supporters to vote despite the court rejecting his plea for a delay. The election follows a tumultuous period marked by an Ebola outbreak and a slump in bauxite prices. Opposition parties had sought a postponement due to alleged electoral roll anomalies, but the election commission refused. Pre-election violence has claimed at least three lives. Conde is favored to win, but a second round of voting is likely. The outcome will determine the country's future after a transition from military to civilian rule in 2010.

Concerns have been raised over the rising use of synthetic drugs within HMP Birmingham, a privately-run prison, which is reportedly leading to violent outbursts and displays of extreme strength among inmates. According to a recent report by the Independent Monitoring Board, covering the period from July 2015 to June this year, the prison continues to show signs of improvement, but the issue of drugs smuggling and staff shortages remains a pressing concern.

The report highlighted the impressive response and support provided by prison staff to inmates, but noted that they regularly face challenges posed by the high rate of sickness and the presence of smuggled drugs. Prison officers at the category B jail have expressed concerns over how to deal with being attacked by inmates under the influence of synthetic drugs, also known as "legal highs". The use of these substances has been linked to at least 19 prisoner deaths between 2012 and 2014, according to the Prisons and Probations Ombudsman.

Rodger Lawrence, chairman of the monitoring board, emphasized the urgent need for a solution to the problem of new psychoactive substances (NPS), which continue to impact all aspects of prison life. He also highlighted staff shortages as a major issue affecting morale, wellbeing, and efficiency. In response, Pete Small, G4S director for HMP Birmingham, acknowledged the challenge of tackling the use of NPS and recognized the work being done by his team in collaboration with the police to catch those bringing drugs into the prison. The prison has vowed to work "relentlessly" to stop the influx of drugs and address the concerns of its staff.

Ian Hutchinson Dominates 600cc Class with Seventh Win

Yorkshire rider Ian Hutchinson led from start to finish to claim his seventh victory in the 600cc class, setting the fastest lap at 128.26mph. Hutchinson, riding for Team Traction Control, built a 10-second lead over his nearest rival, Michael Dunlop, on the opening lap and maintained a steady pace throughout the race. By the end, he had a 14.3-second advantage over Dunlop, who was later disqualified due to a technical infringement.

Dunlop's disqualification moved Dean Harrison up to second place, with James Hillier taking the final podium position. Hutchinson's win was impressive, beating the previous race record by 15.2 seconds. He joins Michael Dunlop as the fourth most successful solo rider in the history of the event.

Hutchinson attributed his success to his connection with the bike, saying, "I seem to have a real connection with this bike and I knew I had to push really hard in the first two sectors." He also acknowledged the challenges posed by backmarkers, stating, "I lost a few seconds here and there after I ran into some backmarkers, but I knew it would be the same for Michael."

The race saw several high-profile retirements, including Peter Hickman and Bruce Anstey. Manxman Conor Cummins and 23-times winner John McGuinness finished fourth and fifth, respectively, with Lee Johnston and William Dunlop taking sixth and seventh positions. The organisers noted that Dunlop's disqualification was due to a technical infringement, but they do not believe it was a deliberate attempt to gain an unfair advantage.

Denbighshire Council Moves Forward with North Wales Hospital Revitalization Plans

The Prince's Regeneration Trust has unveiled proposals for the long-abandoned North Wales Hospital in Denbigh, bringing new hope to the town. Earlier this year, Denbighshire council successfully obtained a compulsory purchase order for the site, citing concerns over the Grade II-listed building's deteriorating state. Although Freemont (Denbigh) Ltd, the current owner, is expected to retain ownership until early 2017, the council plans to transfer the site to the North Wales Buildings Preservation Trust once the ownership changes hands.

The trust, a not-for-profit organization, aims to preserve the historic buildings through "enabling development" plans, which involve generating funds by selling new properties on the site. This approach will allow the trust to balance the need for preservation with the need for financial sustainability. The former Victorian asylum has been vacant since its closure in 1996, and despite Freemont's purchase of the site in 2003, no redevelopment work has taken place.

Denbighshire council has already invested £900,000 in emergency repairs to protect the building from further deterioration. The latest proposals, approved by the council's planning committee, have been met with enthusiasm from local councillor Colin Hughes, who believes the development will bring significant benefits to the town, including an increase in residents and visitors. "The importance of this development to the future of Denbigh is immeasurable," he stated, emphasizing the need to revitalize the site after 21 years of neglect. Despite opposition from Freemont, the council remains committed to moving forward with the plans, marking a new chapter in the hospital's history.

Warrington Wolves dominated St Helens 28-6 at Langtree Park, with Chris Sandow playing a key role in the victory. Sandow's dummy set up Ben Currie for the opening try, before the Australian half-back touched down himself. Ryan Atkins also scored on his 300th career outing, helping Wolves to a 16-0 lead at half-time.

The visitors continued their impressive play in the second half, with Stefan Ratchford and Rhys Evans adding to the score. St Helens' only points came from full-back Jonny Lomax. The loss marks six defeats in eight games for Keiron Cunningham's side, leaving them six points off the top four with six games until the Super 8s.

The match was marred by a long stoppage in play when Jordan Turner received treatment and was carried off on a stretcher. Warrington will look to build on their momentum when they host leaders Hull on June 10. Meanwhile, St Helens will aim to bounce back from their disappointing performance and close the gap on the top four. Referee James Child oversaw the match, which saw Warrington assert their dominance over their rivals.

Aberdeen City and Aberdeenshire councils have taken a significant step towards securing £2.9 billion in funding by submitting a "statement of intent" to the UK and Scottish governments. The statement outlines the benefits that the funding would bring to the city and surrounding area, with a focus on improving infrastructure, boosting the economy, and supporting innovative technologies.

At the top of the councils' list are key projects such as providing more affordable homes, enhancing rail connectivity, and improving links to Aberdeen's harbour and airport. Additionally, research into renewable and hydrogen technologies, as well as international trade, are also highlighted as priorities.

According to Jenny Laing, leader of Aberdeen City Council, the statement of intent provides a solid foundation for a City Region Deal that would not only benefit the north east but also the rest of Scotland and the UK. Laing emphasized the need to work towards a deal that maximizes the benefits of coordinated investment in the Aberdeen city region.

Co-leader of Aberdeenshire Council, Martin Kitts-Hayes, added that the councils will continue to collaborate with the two governments to deliver a City Region Deal that contributes to the economic vision for the north east of Scotland. Kitts-Hayes noted that the region plays a significant role in contributing to the financial wellbeing of Scotland, the UK, and globally, and that greater collaboration across industry and government can help protect the competitiveness of the oil and gas industry and support future growth. A full bid submission is expected to be drawn up by the end of the year.

Tragedy Strikes Construction Site in High Blantyre

A 45-year-old man has lost his life in a fatal incident at a construction site in High Blantyre. Emergency services were called to the Avant Homes site near Shott Farm on Hamilton Road at approximately 09:45. Paramedics treated the seriously injured man, but unfortunately, he died at the scene.

The company has launched an investigation into the incident and suspended all work at the site. The man's identity has not been formally released. Police Scotland has confirmed that the death is not being treated as suspicious at this time, and a post-mortem examination will be conducted to determine the cause of death.

The Health and Safety Executive has been informed, and a report will be submitted to the procurator fiscal. Avant Homes has expressed its condolences to the man's family and loved ones, and is cooperating fully with the emergency services to assist in the investigation.

A takeaway in Edinburgh was targeted by a pair of would-be thieves on Friday night. At 23:00, a man and woman entered the Maysum takeaway on Craigentinny Road, with the man demanding money from staff. After being refused, the pair fled the scene, heading east down Craigentinny Road. Police are investigating and reviewing CCTV footage. The suspects are described as a man in his 20s, 5ft 7in tall, wearing a cream jacket, and a woman, 5ft 9in tall, in a black hooded jacket and pink hat. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Undefeated WBA world super bantamweight champion Guillermo Rigondeaux is set to make his UK debut as he defends his title against Liverpool's Jazza Dickens. The 35-year-old Cuban boxer is widely regarded as one of the world's top pound-for-pound boxers, boasting an impressive record of 16 wins in as many professional bouts. 

Rigondeaux's amateur career was equally impressive, with 475 victories in 487 contests, including gold medals at the 2000 Sydney Olympics and 2004 Athens Olympics. The highly skilled boxer will co-headline a bill featuring WBO world lightweight champion Terry Flanagan's title defense against Mzonke Fana. 

British and Commonwealth super welterweight champion Liam Williams will also be in action, defending his titles against Gary Corcoran in front of his hometown fans in Wales. Rigondeaux's coach, Pedro Diaz, has high praise for his fighter, calling him "the most complete" boxer in the world. With his unique ability to only fight boxers with winning records, Rigondeaux is poised to put on a show in his UK debut. Fans are eagerly anticipating the event, which promises to be an exciting night of boxing.

CCTV footage of a heist outside Debenhams has been released. A man stole a cashbox from a security van on Monday at 14:15 GMT. Police seek witnesses and are tracing a silver van abandoned in Russell Street. No weapons were used and no one was injured in the incident.

Ikea to Recall 1.7 Million Drawers in China Over Safety Concerns

China's regulator has announced that Ikea will recall 1.7 million drawers due to safety concerns. The decision comes after six children in North America were crushed to death when the chests toppled on them. The recall affects drawers made between 1999 and 2016. 

Last month, Ikea recalled 36 million dressers in the US and Canada, and has since stopped selling the drawers. Initially, the company refused to extend the recall to China, the UK, or the EU, citing that the products met local industry standards. However, following an online backlash in China and a meeting with the country's safety watchdog, Ikea has agreed to the recall.

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission found that the Malm drawers can topple over and crush children if not anchored to the wall with screws. Ikea has warned customers to ensure the drawers are properly fixed to walls and has launched an awareness campaign. The company has also offered free home installation and an optional refund to customers in China. Ikea has pledged to "serve as a model" in responding to the challenge of furniture safety. The recall highlights the importance of ensuring household safety and the need for companies to prioritize consumer well-being.

A former paramedic, Andrew Davies, has been found guilty of misconduct by a health profession panel for failing to assist a man who later died of a heart attack. The incident occurred in the car park of Walsall Manor Hospital in June 2012, where 47-year-old Carl Cope was in need of medical attention. Despite the presence of four clinical staff members, including Davies, no aid was provided to Mr. Cope.

The Health and Care Professions Council panel heard that Davies had been previously dismissed by his employer, West Midlands Ambulance Service, for gross misconduct. The panel chair, Naseem Malik, stated that Davies' inaction was "conduct falling far below that expected by the public, his profession, and fellow practitioners." Due to a lack of insight into his mistakes, the panel deemed it likely that Davies could repeat such misconduct in the future.

As a result, Davies was struck off the HCPC Register, effectively ending his career as a paramedic. This ruling comes after another paramedic, Matthew Geary, received an eight-month suspended jail term for his role in failing to provide adequate treatment to Mr. Cope. The case highlights the importance of medical professionals providing timely and adequate care to those in need, and the severe consequences that can result from failing to do so.

Celebrities React to Dallas Shootings, Call for Peace and an End to Violence

The recent shootings in Dallas, which left five police officers dead and several others injured, have sparked an outpouring of reactions from celebrities across the United States. The shootings occurred during a protest against the use of lethal force by police against African Americans, and have reignited a national debate about racism and violence.

John Legend, who won an Oscar for his song "Glory" from the film Selma, was among the first to speak out against the violence. "Being against cops killing is not equal to being for killing cops. We need peace in our streets," he tweeted. Legend also condemned the shootings, calling them "horrific" and "morally reprehensible."

Other celebrities, including Beyonce and Jay-Z, have also reacted to the shootings. Beyonce held a minute's silence at her concert in Glasgow on Thursday night for the two black men, Alton Sterling and Philando Castile, who were killed by police earlier in the week. She also put their names on a big screen and pleaded for an end to the "war on minorities" in the US.

Jay-Z released a new song, "Spiritual," on his streaming service Tidal, and released a statement saying that he was "saddened and disappointed" by the events in the US. "I'm saddened and disappointed in THIS America - we should be further along. WE ARE NOT," he said. He also sent blessings to the families of those who "lost loved ones to police brutality."

Michael Moore, who directed the documentary "Bowling for Columbine," tweeted that President Obama's presence was needed to address the crisis. "We need our President to speak to the nation, to address the racism and the violence that is tearing our country apart," he said.

Oscar-winning actress Patricia Arquette added her voice to the chorus of condemnation, saying "Just heard about shootings in Dallas Please everyone stop killing each other- no more guns. No more violence. No more murder. Horrible."

Other celebrities, including Kevin Hart, Justin Timberlake, and Katy Perry, have also spoken out against the violence. Hart tweeted "Peace is the message.... An eye for an eye leaves everybody blind," while Timberlake said "This IS systemic. We MUST DO BETTER. My heart goes out to the families of #AltonSterling and #PhilandoCastile May they both Rest In Peace."

Katy Perry linked to a video of Alton Sterling being shot, saying "You can't just go on with your day, you must watch this & we must face this continual outrageousness #ALTONSTERLING." Canadian rapper Drake also spoke out, saying that it was "impossible to ignore" the strained relationship between black and brown communities and law enforcement.

The shootings in Dallas have sparked a national conversation about racism and violence, and it is clear that many celebrities are committed to using their platforms to call for peace and an end to violence. As Cynthia Erivo, who won a Tony for her portrayal of Celie in Broadway's The Color Purple, tweeted, "Dear Lord I ask you to take this world in your arms and brush it with love and peace and understanding. It's gone too far."

Edinburgh Rugby Team Secures Crucial Win Against Zebre, Moves into Fifth Place

In a thrilling match at Murrayfield, Edinburgh Rugby Team managed to secure a crucial win against Zebre, moving into fifth place in the league standings. The team's victory was largely due to a strong second-half performance, which saw them score 24 unanswered points against their Italian opponents.

The first half of the game was a dismal affair, with Edinburgh managing to score only three points from the boot of Jason Tovey. The team's performance was marred by errors, with fumbles, stray passes, and petty squabbles dominating the opening 40 minutes. Zebre's Kelly Haimona also missed a penalty attempt, and the visitors were denied a try when Oliviero Fabiani's route was cleared by an obstruction.

However, the introduction of Sam Hidalgo-Clyne in the second half brought a much-needed spark to the game. The replacement scrum-half threaded a grubber through for Damien Hoyland to run onto, and the winger was able to kick it on and win the race for the line. This try was the catalyst for Edinburgh's dominance in the second half, with Hoyland scoring again soon after.

Tovey converted both of Hoyland's tries and also made it three from three when his clever break was supported well by Stuart McInally, with the replacement hooker offloading for Hidalgo-Clyne to waltz through unchallenged. The home team's chances of securing a try bonus point seemed to have slipped away when a late penalty was kicked into touch, only for Zebre to rob the line-out. However, an offside infringement allowed Edinburgh to keep the ball alive, and a patient passing move was finished off by Ben Toolis.

Edinburgh's win moves them ahead of Glasgow and Munster into fifth place, with those teams in action on Saturday. If Alan Solomons' side is to hang on to a top-six spot and earn a Champions Cup place, they will need to turn in more performances like their second-half showing at Murrayfield. The team's error-strewn opening 40 minutes was a concern, but their ability to turn the game around in the second half will give them confidence going into their next match.

The final score was 24-0 in favor of Edinburgh, with Tovey's conversions and penalties proving crucial in the team's victory. Hidalgo-Clyne's introduction was also a key factor, bringing a much-needed zip to the game and setting up two of Edinburgh's tries. The team will look to build on this performance in their next match, as they aim to secure a top-six spot and a place in the Champions Cup.

In terms of team selection, Edinburgh started with a strong lineup, featuring the likes of Jason Tovey, Damien Hoyland, and WP Nel. The team's replacements, including Sam Hidalgo-Clyne and Stuart McInally, also made a significant impact on the game. Zebre, on the other hand, struggled to cope with Edinburgh's pressure in the second half, and their ill-discipline ultimately cost them the game.

Referee Leighton Hodges had a busy game, with several penalties and infringements to contend with. However, his decisions ultimately had little impact on the outcome of the match, as Edinburgh's superior performance in the second half secured them the win. Overall, it was a crucial victory for Edinburgh, and one that will give them confidence going into their next match.

The Metropolitan Police's counter-terrorism command is seeking to recruit former jihadists who have abandoned radicalism to help combat terrorist propaganda. According to Commander Richard Walton, these individuals can serve as "powerful voices" in challenging the ideology of militant groups such as Islamic State. The Met is "desperate" to find more former extremists to aid in their efforts, with only a few currently working with them.

In the past year, the Met's counter-terrorism command has seen a significant increase in arrests, with 225 people detained on suspicion of terrorism-related offences - a 32% rise from the previous year. Notably, 29 of those arrested were women or girls, and 17 were under the age of 20. The Met has also successfully rescued several families, including young children, who were attempting to travel to Syria from Turkey.

Commander Walton emphasized the importance of engaging with terrorists, even those in prison, in an effort to turn them away from extremism. He noted that some individuals convicted of terrorist offences may not have received lengthy sentences and will eventually be released, presenting an opportunity for the Met to work with them. The goal is to develop "counter-narratives" to challenge Islamic State's ideology, with the help of former extremists. With at least 700 people from the UK having travelled to support or fight for jihadist organisations in Syria and Iraq, the Met's efforts to counter terrorist propaganda are more crucial than ever.

A house in Birmingham's Handsworth Wood area was evacuated after a marijuana grow operation sparked an electrical fire. Fire crews responded to the incident on Hamstead Hall Avenue at 06:50 GMT on Sunday. They found a severely overloaded fuse box and a large stash of marijuana. The scene was likened to a Cheech and Chong movie set. Authorities warned that the setup posed a huge threat to public safety, putting neighbors at risk of damage or death due to the hazardous conditions. The West Midlands Police Cannabis Disposal Team is investigating.

A fatal collision occurred on the Shrivenham Bypass near Swindon, killing four people in their 20s from Northampton. The occupants of the other vehicle, including a three-year-old, were injured and hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Thames Valley Police are investigating and urge witnesses to come forward.

Edinburgh Rugby Club is facing an injury crisis ahead of their upcoming Pro12 match against Connacht in Galway on Friday. Stand-off Duncan Weir, 25, underwent surgery on Sunday after a clash of heads with CJ Stander and will be out of action for some time. Fellow stand-off Jason Tovey has made a timely return to training from a wrist injury, but inside centre Phil Burleigh, who can also play at fly-half, is still recovering from a shoulder injury.

The club's prop situation is also a concern, with Kevin Bryce awaiting the results of a scan on an elbow injury he suffered in the first scrum against Munster. Simon Berghan is still several weeks away from returning from a foot injury, leaving Nick Beavon as the only back-up to WP Nel. Head coach Alan Solomons is keen to bring in extra tight-head cover to alleviate the pressure.

In the meantime, 19-year-old Blair Kinghorn, who replaced Weir in Limerick, could feature at 10 against Connacht. The team has also been dealt a blow with the loss of third-choice hooker George Turner, who sustained an ankle injury playing for Heriot's in the BT Premiership. However, back-row Nasi Manu has returned to training after recovering from a rib injury.

The club is also awaiting the outcome of a citing for lock Fraser McKenzie, who was involved in a shoulder charge incident against Munster. A decision is expected on Wednesday. Loose-head prop Alasdair Dickinson is on track to return to training in late October, which will be a welcome boost ahead of Scotland's autumn Tests. With several key players out injured, Edinburgh will be looking to dig deep and find a way to overcome Connacht on Friday.

A 28-year-old man is in critical condition after being assaulted by two men in Union Street. The incident occurred at approximately 05:30, between St Nicholas Street and Broad Street. The victim was taken to the Royal Infirmary with serious injuries. Police are seeking information about the attackers, describing one as 6ft tall with dark hair, wearing a grey T-shirt and dark jeans. The second man is described as 5ft 9in tall with short grey hair, wearing a brown bomber-style jacket and dark blue jeans. Detective Inspector Norman Stevenson is urging witnesses to come forward, appealing for anyone who saw the attack to contact the police and provide information about what they saw.

Energy Giants Consider Reward Programs for Loyal Customers

In a bid to address the issue of millions of customers paying too much for energy, two of the UK's major energy suppliers, Npower and EDF Energy, are considering introducing reward programs for their loyal customers. The move comes after pressure from Business Secretary Greg Clark, who suggested that customers who have been on standard variable tariffs for a long time should be rewarded for their loyalty.

Npower's managing director of domestic markets, Simon Stacey, revealed that the company is actively exploring the idea of offering rewards to its standard customers, such as a free boiler service. "We want to try and reward customers in a way they wouldn't expect," he told the Business and Energy Committee. EDF Energy's residential sales director, Dan Hopcroft, also confirmed that his company is looking at introducing a loyalty proposition.

The move is aimed at the estimated 10 million customers who have been on expensive standard tariffs for at least three years. According to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), 56% of consumers have never switched supplier or are unsure if they have. The CMA has been pushing for reforms in the energy market to encourage more customers to switch to cheaper deals.

In a separate development, energy regulator Ofgem has announced plans to conduct trials to test new ways of persuading reluctant customers to switch suppliers. The trials, which are expected to start later this year, will involve tens of thousands of consumers and will explore different approaches, such as renaming standard tariffs to "emergency tariff" or "out-of-contract tariff". Suppliers will also be asked to inform customers about cheaper deals available from rival suppliers.

The trials are part of a broader effort to increase transparency and competition in the energy market. Currently, suppliers are only required to show their own cheapest tariff on bills, but not the tariffs of their competitors. By introducing reward programs and testing new approaches to encourage switching, energy suppliers are hoping to address the issue of loyal customers paying too much for their energy.

Fulham Secures Crucial Victory Over Cardiff, Moves 10 Points Clear of Relegation Zone

In a thrilling match at Craven Cottage, Fulham secured a vital 2-1 victory over Cardiff City, thanks to a late winner from Emerson Hyndman in stoppage time. The win moves Fulham 10 points clear of the relegation zone, while Cardiff remains five points adrift of the Championship play-off places with only five games remaining.

The match got off to a lively start, with both sides creating scoring opportunities in the first half. Aron Gunnarsson's header was saved by Marcus Bettinelli, while Bruno Ecuele Manga headed over from Peter Whittingham's corner. At the other end, David Marshall parried a free-kick from former Cardiff striker Ross McCormack.

Cardiff took the lead in the 25th minute when Scott Malone combined with Gunnarsson down the left, and the Icelandic midfielder's cross was met by Lex Immers, who headed home his fifth goal of the season. However, Fulham levelled the score in the opening minute of the second half, catching Cardiff's defence off guard. Moussa Dembele set up former England midfielder Scott Parker, who fired home from a tight angle to score his first goal of the season.

The second half saw Fulham gain momentum, with Dembele and McCormack creating scoring opportunities. Gunnarsson and Sean Morrison squandered chances for Cardiff, who struggled to replicate their first-half performance. As the match drew to a close, Fulham's pressure finally paid off when Hyndman struck from close range following a scramble at a corner in stoppage time.

Fulham boss Slavisa Jokanovic expressed his delight at the win, saying, "Today is Emerson Hyndman's birthday, and it's a great present for himself and for all of us in the last moment of the game. He's probably one of the more talented players, and I am little bit disappointed with myself that I haven't found more minutes for him this season." Jokanovic also acknowledged that while the win was crucial, there is still work to be done to ensure safety. "We've had one perfect week where we've won three games, but in front of us is five games more. Mathematically, we are 10 points ahead, but we need five points more to be 100 per cent sure."

Cardiff City manager Russell Slade was left to ponder what might have been, saying, "We will keep going to the end. It's a setback, and we would have taken a precious point. We've given ourselves a mountain to climb, but there's still time to go." Slade acknowledged that a draw would have been a fair result but was frustrated that his side failed to defend a corner, which led to Hyndman's winner. Despite the setback, Slade remains optimistic, saying, "We've had some real high-level performances recently, and where we want to be is certainly not impossible. We'll keep going, and we've got a home game next week, and all we can control is what's in front of us."

The win is a significant boost for Fulham, who have now won three consecutive games. As they look to secure their Championship status, they will be eager to build on this momentum in their remaining five games. For Cardiff, the task ahead is daunting, but Slade's side will be determined to bridge the gap and make a late push for the play-offs.

A disturbing incident occurred on the Britwell estate in Slough, where two young boys, aged six and 10, were abducted from a property on Hemming Way. The offenders, wearing dark clothing and with their faces covered, entered the property between 7:00 and 7:30 GMT and ordered the boys into a white van parked outside. The vehicle travelled to Upper Lees Road, where the boys managed to escape and run back to Hemming Way, fortunately uninjured. Police are currently investigating the motive behind the abduction, with Detective Inspector Nicola Hurdley stating that the incident is "understandably upsetting" for the victims and their relatives. The suspects' van is believed to be a Ford Transit, and officers are appealing for witnesses to come forward with any information. Police are providing support to the affected families as they work to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Russia's central bank has lowered its one-week minimum auction repo rate by 1 percentage point. This decision comes as inflation eased to 15.8% in May, down from 16.9% in March. The bank expressed concern over the economy's "considerable" cooling, predicting a 3.2% contraction in gross domestic product this year. The rate cut was in line with analyst expectations, resulting in little change to the Russian rouble. Western sanctions and falling global oil prices continue to squeeze Russia's economy, which had led to an emergency interest rate hike to 17% last December to stabilize the rouble.

High Court Ruling Paves Way for Resumption of Troubles-Related Inquests

A long-awaited ruling at the High Court in Belfast has brought an end to a legal challenge by relatives of victims of the Troubles, clearing the way for the resumption of inquests into their loved ones' deaths. The inquests, which were ordered by Attorney General John Larkin, were halted last November by senior coroner John Leckey, who questioned whether he had exceeded his powers in authorizing the hearings.

The move sparked outrage among the families, who claimed that the decision was unlawful and procedurally unfair. Lawyers for the families launched a judicial review challenge, which was due to be heard next week. However, the challenge has now been formally ended, paving the way for the inquests to resume.

The inquests will examine the deaths of several individuals, including 11-year-old Francis Rowntree, who was killed by a rubber bullet fired by a soldier in 1972, and Gerard Slane, a 27-year-old father of three who was shot dead by the Ulster Defence Association in 1988. The killings of Gerard Casey, Danny Doherty, William Fleming, and Francis Bradley will also be scrutinized.

Outside the court, solicitor Paul Pierce, representing Mr. Slane's widow Teresa, welcomed the decision to lift the suspension on the inquests. "We are pleased that the coroner has lifted the suspension, and we look forward to the inquests proceeding," he said. John Teggart, whose father was killed in the 1970s in Ballymurphy, also spoke out, saying that questions need to be answered about the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

The resumption of the inquests is a significant development in the ongoing quest for truth and justice by the families of those who died during the Troubles. The hearings are expected to shed new light on the circumstances surrounding the deaths and may provide long-awaited closure for the families. With the legal challenge now at an end, the families can finally begin to get the answers they have been seeking for so long.

As the UK general election heats up, Labour MPs from the left-wing faction are considering challenging the party's first Queen's Speech, potentially joining forces with the Scottish National Party to oppose cuts. This revelation comes after an interview with John McDonnell, leader of the Socialist Campaign Group, published in the New Statesman. The move could signal a significant rift within the party and potentially jeopardize the passage of key legislation.

Meanwhile, Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg is reportedly preparing to demand a "steep price" from the Conservatives in exchange for supporting a referendum on British membership of the EU in the event of a hung parliament. The Financial Times reports that Clegg is seeking to extract significant concessions from the Tories, potentially paving the way for a power-sharing deal.

On the campaign trail, Conservative leader David Cameron has come under fire for his claims that families will face a £3,000 tax rise if Labour is elected. The Institute for Fiscal Studies has disputed the claim, undermining Cameron's argument. The Guardian leads with the story, highlighting the ongoing debate over the economy and taxation.

In other news, Ed Miliband's credibility on economic issues has taken a hit after business leaders expressed concerns over the use of their quotes in a Labour party advert. The Telegraph reports that the controversy has raised questions about the party's judgment and ability to manage the economy.

As the election approaches, minor party candidates are also making their voices heard. Plaid Cymru leader Leanne Wood has launched her party's manifesto, criticizing the main parties for offering "nothing more than further swingeing cuts" to public services. SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon has also reiterated her opposition to the renewal of Trident, stating that it is a "red line" for her party. With the election just around the corner, the battle for votes is intensifying, and all parties are pulling out the stops to win over undecided voters.

The notorious online drugs marketplace, Silk Road, has been shut down following a lengthy investigation by the National Cyber Crime Unit (NCCU). The interim head of the NCCU, Andy Archibald, revealed that officers were able to identify individuals using the site, but warned that new methods are needed to keep up with the evolving threat of online crime.

The success of the operation may not be easily replicated, according to Archibald, as online anonymity services like Tor continually update and resecure themselves. The NCCU will need to adapt and find new ways to infiltrate and disrupt criminal forums. Archibald's comments came as the NCCU announced its first conviction, with 27-year-old Olukunle Babatunde receiving a five year and six month prison sentence for using "phishing" scams to attempt to defraud banks and financial institutions. The conviction marks a significant milestone for the NCCU as it continues to tackle online crime.

Indian Cricketer Ravindra Jadeja Under Investigation for Breaking Safari Rules

Indian cricketer Ravindra Jadeja is under investigation for allegedly breaking rules at the Gir National Park and Sanctuary in Gujarat. Photos posted on his Instagram account appear to show him and his wife, Reeva, on foot during a safari, pointing to a pride of lions and taking a photo with one in the background. However, officials at the park stated that it is against the rules for visitors to leave their vehicles, and a penalty may be imposed.

The Gir National Park is the only home of the Asiatic lion in the wild, and the animals are listed as endangered. Just days before Jadeja's visit, forestry officials had warned of the dangers of taking selfies with lions. Chief Forest Conservator AP Singh has ordered a probe into the matter, which will consider what penalty to impose on the couple. Jadeja, 27, was part of India's team for the recent World T20 tournament. The incident has sparked concern over the safety and well-being of both the visitors and the animals at the park.

Serge Gnabry has completed a transfer to Werder Bremen, leaving Arsenal after five years. The 21-year-old was joint top scorer at the Olympic Games with six goals. Gnabry made 18 appearances for Arsenal, scoring once, before making the move. Initially, reports suggested a transfer to Bayern Munich with a subsequent loan to Bremen, but the club's sporting director denied any other club's involvement. Gnabry expressed confidence in his new team, citing positive comments from Per Mertesacker and Mesut Ozil. He also praised his talks with management, which led to his decision to join Bremen. Gnabry aims for a successful season, targeting the top half of the table.

Maldives in Crisis: Former President Claims Coup, Successor Denies Allegations

The island nation of Maldives is reeling from a deepening political crisis, with former President Mohamed Nasheed claiming he was forced to resign in a coup orchestrated by his successor, President Mohammed Waheed Hassan. In a dramatic turn of events, Nasheed told the AFP news agency that he was coerced into stepping down by armed police and army officers, who threatened to use violence if he refused.

According to Nasheed, he was summoned to military headquarters on Tuesday, where he found a group of 18 middle-ranking police and army officers in control. "They told me if I didn't resign, they would resort to using arms," he said, describing the encounter as a thinly veiled threat. Fearing for the safety of his government officials, Nasheed reluctantly agreed to step down.

However, President Hassan has categorically denied any involvement in a coup, stating that Nasheed's resignation was a "generous decision" that helped prevent bloodshed. Hassan, who served as Nasheed's vice president before taking over the presidency, criticized his predecessor for wrongfully arresting a top judge, Abdulla Mohamed, last month.

The arrest of Judge Mohamed sparked widespread protests, with many calling for Nasheed's resignation. The judge, who was accused of being loyal to the opposition, was released soon after Hassan took power. Hassan has promised to respect the rule of law, uphold the constitution, and protect Nasheed from retribution, while also vowing not to interfere with any police or court action against his predecessor.

As the political crisis deepens, concerns are growing for the safety of Nasheed and other senior members of his government. Nasheed's supporters fear that he may face retribution, and there are reports of an investigation into the discovery of bottles of alcohol being removed from outside his residence. Consuming alcohol outside tourist resorts is a crime in the Muslim nation.

In an effort to stabilize the country, President Hassan has called for the formation of a national unity government, which he believes can help bring "calm and quiet to the streets." He has also pledged to hold elections in 2013, which would lead to the formation of a new government.

The crisis in Maldives has sparked international concern, with many calling for a peaceful resolution to the conflict. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen whether President Hassan's efforts to build a stable and democratic country will be successful, or if the nation will slide further into chaos. One thing is certain, however: the fate of former President Nasheed and the future of Maldives hang precariously in the balance.

The Unsung Heroes of Formula 1: A Tribute to the Brave and Dedicated Marshals

As the Formula 1 season comes to a close, it's time to shine the spotlight on the unsung heroes of the sport: the marshals. These dedicated volunteers give up their free time to ensure the smooth running of every Grand Prix, often putting themselves in harm's way to keep the drivers and spectators safe.

From the early morning hours to long after sunset, marshals are on duty, ready to respond to any incident on the track. Their quick thinking and swift action have been instrumental in minimizing delays and keeping the racing action going. This season has seen its fair share of close calls, with marshals narrowly avoiding being hit by speeding cars, including a heart-stopping moment in Russia when a marshal sprinted onto the track just seconds before Sebastian Vettel's Ferrari flew by.

Marshals also have to contend with unpredictable weather conditions, as seen during the United States Grand Prix, where they were evacuated due to the risk of lightning strikes. Despite these challenges, they remain steadfast and dedicated, always putting the safety of others first. While their role is often thankless, they occasionally get to let their hair down, such as wearing masks during practice sessions near Halloween or staging mock pitstops with the safety car.

It's a testament to their bravery and dedication that the on-track action has rarely been delayed for long this season. As the Formula 1 community looks back on another thrilling season, it's time to give a well-deserved tribute to the marshals, who are truly the stars of the show. Their selflessness, quick thinking, and passion for the sport make them the unsung heroes of Formula 1.

A suspect package report prompted the closure of Swansea's Indoor Market and bus station. South Wales Police reopened the areas at 17:00 BST after investigating. The incident caused significant disruption, but bus services are resuming. Police warned of robust action against hoax activity, urging vigilance while minimizing unnecessary disruption to the community.

Great Wall Motors, China's largest SUV manufacturer, has expressed interest in acquiring some or all of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA), the world's seventh-largest car maker. According to a Great Wall official, the company has "an intention to acquire" FCA, although Fiat Chrysler has yet to receive a formal approach. The news sent shares in FCA soaring 7.4% in New York on Monday, with the company's valuation now standing at over $19 billion.

The potential acquisition has sparked speculation that Great Wall is primarily interested in FCA's most valuable asset: the Jeep brand. Jeep, which celebrated its 75th birthday last year, is a iconic brand with a reputation dating back to World War Two, when its vehicles were extensively used by the US military. Morgan Stanley analysts estimate that the Jeep brand alone could be worth as much as $27 billion, making it a highly prized asset for any potential buyer.

The potential takeover has also raised concerns in the White House, with President Trump having previously expressed concerns about China's growing economic influence. His former chief strategist, Steve Bannon, has gone so far as to describe the US as being in an "economic war" with China. While Great Wall's acquisition of FCA may not have an immediate impact on US jobs, as the company could choose to maintain manufacturing operations in the US, it is likely that the Chinese firm is primarily interested in acquiring Jeep's technology and engineering expertise.

This has raised eyebrows, given that President Trump has ordered an investigation into allegations of China's theft of US intellectual property. The potential for the takeover to add to the friction between the US and China is high, particularly if the deal is seen as a strategic move by China to acquire valuable US technology and expertise.

According to Bill Russo, a former Chrysler executive, Great Wall is likely interested in acquiring the Jeep brand rather than all of FCA, which has debts of around $4.9 billion. "Jeep is the crown jewel of Fiat Chrysler in terms of brand and equity," he said. "A deal would be quite complementary, given Great Wall's focus on SUVs." Yale Zhang, head of Shanghai-based consultancy Automotive Foresight, agrees, stating that "Jeep is the most logical choice, since [Great Wall] wants to be the largest SUV maker in the world."

FCA's chief executive, Sergio Marchionne, has been seeking a partner or buyer to help the company manage rising costs, emissions regulations, and the development of electric and self-driving cars. The company also owns Alfa Romeo, Maserati, and RAM trucks, although it is unclear whether Great Wall would be interested in acquiring these brands as part of a potential deal.

As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen whether Great Wall's acquisition of FCA will come to fruition. However, one thing is clear: the potential takeover has significant implications for the global automotive industry, and could have far-reaching consequences for the US-China trade relationship. With Great Wall's ambition to become the world's largest SUV maker, and FCA's need for a partner to help navigate the challenges of the modern automotive industry, a deal could be seen as a strategic move by both parties. However, it is likely to face close scrutiny from regulators and politicians on both sides of the Pacific.

The Scarlets have secured the services of their attack coach, Stephen Hayward, on a new contract. Hayward joined the region in August 2014, bringing his experience from coaching the Wales Under-20 side. He praised head coach Wayne Pivac, who also recently signed a two-year deal, for allowing him to take the reins from the start.
